A young woman holds a jar of water that pours into a spring, standing gracefully against a rocky background. Ingres first worked on this for years, and the final version was completed in 1856 with help from his students. It became a symbol of purity and the natural spring of life. It was a hit with the public and remained a favorite of French painting for generations.

paintings.t: A Journalist Lecturing on the Orrery
paintings.why: A lecturer shows a model of the solar system, called an orrery, to a group of people gathered around a lamp that stands for the Sun. Wright painted the awe on their faces as they learn how planets move. The painting celebrated science at a time when new ideas were exciting everyone. It's famous for making learning look as dramatic as an adventure.

paintings.m: Department of Paintings of the Louvre
paintings.why: In 1822 Greek islanders suffered a terrible attack during their war for independence, and Delacroix painted the grief and suffering that followed. The painting is full of weary survivors in a sweeping landscape, shown with deep sympathy. French viewers were moved, and it helped build support for the Greek cause. It also made Delacroix a leader of the Romantic movement.

Ruins of an abbey rise in a misty twilight, with bare oak trees and a quiet funeral procession of monks. Friedrich was interested in mortality and faith, and he painted this gloomy, moving scene when he was in his thirties. It helped make him a star of German Romanticism. It's remembered for its mysterious, hushed mood.

A young woman reclines on a green couch in a white gown with a golden sash, gazing out confidently. Goya painted this as a twin to the famous nude version, and each could be switched in a hidden frame. It's famous for its sparkling fabric and for the mystery of who she was. It's still one of the best-loved works in Madrid's Prado Museum.

A young couple shares a passionate kiss on a staircase as the man prepares to leave on a journey. Hayez painted it to express the Italian wish for freedom, because it was a time when Italians were fighting for unity. Look at the shimmering blue dress, which became one of the most famous patches of color in Italian art. It's loved as a symbol of love and patriotism.

Great jagged slabs of ice are heaped like a shattered ship against a pale polar sky. Friedrich painted this icy world to show how powerful nature can be, and how small people are. Hidden in the ice is the wreck of a ship, a reminder of human limits. It's one of the great paintings of nature's wild beauty.

Four people stand on a balcony in green shutters, looking out in different directions as if lost in thoughts. Manet was inspired by a painting by Goya, and the flat, bold colors were thought odd in 1869. The figures don't speak to each other, which gives a modern, mysterious feeling. The painter Berthe Morisot, an Impressionist herself, sits in front.

A woman sleeps in the desert under a full moon while a lion sniffs at her and walks away. Rousseau painted it with flat, dreamlike shapes and strange calm. He had no formal training, so his art has a childlike purity. It's famous as a masterpiece of 'naive' art and a forerunner of surrealism.

A proud young woman in a dark velvet hat and furs looks down at us from an open carriage on a snowy street. Kramskoi never said who she was, so she's remained a mystery. Her glowing face and confident gaze make her one of the most famous faces in Russian art. People still wonder about her story.

paintings.m: Department of Paintings of the Louvre
paintings.why: Dozens of women are crowded together in a circular steamy bathhouse in this unusual round painting. Ingres finished it when he was 82, and it's considered a final masterpiece of his career. It was inspired by stories from travelers. The unusual circular shape resembles a view through a keyhole.

paintings.m: Department of Paintings of the Louvre
paintings.why: Dante and the Roman poet Virgil cross a stormy river in the underworld in a little boat while tortured souls cling to the sides. Delacroix was only 24, and this painting launched his career. The dark drama and strong colors were a daring change from the calmer art of the time. It's remembered as the first great Romantic painting.

As the volcano Vesuvius erupts, the people of ancient Pompeii run in terror under falling stones and lightning. Bryullov spent years researching the real ruins to make it accurate. When it was shown in Italy and Russia, crowds cheered and the writer Pushkin praised it. It's famous for combining drama with real history.

A stylish Parisian socialite stands in a plunging black dress, her skin pale and her head turned in profile. When Sargent showed it in 1884, people were scandalized — especially because one dress strap had slipped off her shoulder. He repainted it to the right place, but the damage to his Paris career was done. Today it's one of the greatest portraits of elegance and confidence.

paintings.t: An Experiment on a Bird in the Air Pump
paintings.why: A scientist pumps the air out of a glass jar holding a white cockatoo as the family watches, some fascinated and some upset. Wright painted it by candlelight to build suspense, asking whether science is always right. It's a rare painting that makes a science experiment feel like a thrilling drama. It sits among the most famous works of the Enlightenment.

Three women bend over in a golden field to gather leftover grain after the harvest, while far behind them workers pile up huge stacks of wheat. Gleaning was the work of the very poor, and Millet gave them heroic, monumental dignity. Some wealthy viewers disliked it, but today it's treasured. It is a landmark of respect for working people.

paintings.t: Rain, Steam and Speed – The Great Western Railway
paintings.why: A steam train rushes toward us across a bridge through a misty, golden haze of rain and light. Turner painted it when railways were brand-new and thrilling, and he captured the feeling of speed. A tiny hare runs ahead of the engine. It's loved as a glimpse of the modern world arriving.

A crowd of Parisians chat and listen to a concert under tall trees in the Tuileries Garden. Manet painted his friends, including poets, musicians and fellow artists. The faces are dabbed in quickly, which was daring at the time. It's celebrated as one of the first paintings of modern city life in Paris.

In the streets of Madrid, citizens rise up with knives against Napoleon's mounted soldiers. Goya painted this and its companion, 'The Third of May', six years later to honor the people who fought. The chaotic fight swirls with horses and flashing blades. It's a landmark of war painting that focuses on ordinary people.

In a gothic workshop, an alchemist falls to his knees with astonishment as a strange glow rises in his flask — the discovery of phosphorus, which glows in the dark. Wright painted the pale glow as though it were magic. The picture celebrates the thrill of discovery. It's a marvelous example of dramatic lighting.

A tall dark cypress tree reaches up between a glowing crescent moon and a bright star, while travelers walk along a winding road below. Van Gogh painted this in 1890, one of his last great paintings. The swirling sky and flame-like tree give a sense of energy. It captures his love of the night.

paintings.t: Skull of a Skeleton with Burning Cigarette
paintings.why: A skeleton's skull seems to puff on a cigarette in this funny, spooky, and thoughtful painting. Van Gogh was a young art student in Antwerp when he painted it, likely as a student joke. Skulls have long been used in art to remind us that life is short. It's become one of his most reproduced images.

George Washington stands boldly in a boat full of soldiers crossing an icy river on Christmas night in 1776, before a surprise attack on enemy troops. Leutze painted it in Germany, and it's much larger than a car. Experts note details that aren't accurate, but it became the best-known picture of the American Revolution. It's a classic example of heroic history painting.

Two men watch in horror as a demon-like figure bites a man in a fight between damned souls in Hell, taken from Dante's poem. Bouguereau was young when he painted this, and its strong, twisted bodies show his skill. It's less gentle than his famous later works. It's remembered as a dramatic and daring early success.

A sunny terrace overlooks a sparkling sea with sailboats, with a family relaxing among bright flowers. Monet painted it when he was 27 at his aunt's home on the Normandy coast. The bold, flat blocks of color show the influence of Japanese prints. It's an early, joyful look at the Impressionist style.

A young woman in a glowing orange dress is curled up asleep in a sunny courtyard, with the sea behind her. Leighton used the vivid color to suggest the heat of summer. For years the painting was forgotten and even sold cheaply, and then rediscovered. Today it's one of the most loved Victorian paintings, and it now hangs in a museum in Puerto Rico.

A girl on a swing and some friends are caught in dappled sunlight filtering through the trees. Renoir painted blotches of blue shadow on the white dress, which some critics scoffed at as dirty! We now see it as a brilliant study of light. It's one of the happiest Impressionist works.

A little white house glows in the blue dusk with lighted windows, under a dark tree and a deep blue sky. Van Gogh painted this in 1890 in Auvers-sur-Oise during his final weeks. The warm light pouring from the windows feels like a welcome home. It remains one of his cozy, quiet nighttime scenes.

In a Greek myth, the princess Danaë was shut in a tower and visited by Zeus in a shower of gold. Klimt painted her curled up while the gold rains down. The shimmering patterns and rich colors show his signature style. It's one of the most famous mythological paintings of the early 1900s.

Figures arch like a cathedral around a lake, their bodies simplified into solid blocks and triangles of blue and green. Cézanne worked on his big bather paintings for years and left this one near the end of his life. It paved the way for Cubism and modern art. Picasso and Matisse studied it closely.

paintings.t: Woman with a Parasol – Madame Monet and Her Son
paintings.why: A woman and a young boy stand on a breezy hilltop, with the sunlit sky behind them. Monet painted his wife Camille and their son Jean out of doors, with fast brushstrokes to catch the wind and light. We see her from below, so she seems to float against the clouds. It's a delight of the Impressionist movement.

A woman lies on her back playing with a parrot perched on her hand, her hair flowing loosely. Courbet painted her with realistic detail, when the Salon expected idealized goddesses. It was both admired and criticized. It became a highlight of the Metropolitan Museum's French collection.

A kind art-supply dealer sits in front of a wall of Japanese woodblock prints, wearing a straw hat and a calm smile. Père Tanguy supported struggling artists like Van Gogh, who painted him in bright colors. It shows how much Van Gogh admired Japanese art. It's a rare, happy portrait of a good friend.

A quiet bare garden stands in front of a church in the Netherlands, where Van Gogh's father was a pastor. He painted it in earthy, muted tones when he was a young artist, before his famous bright colors. The painting was stolen from a Dutch museum in 2020 and was recovered a few years later. It's a quiet look at his early life.

A woman stands in the surf as waves roll against a stormy sky. Courbet painted the sea many times and loved its raw power. The painting was shown in Paris in 1868 and was praised for its realism. It captures the thrill of the ocean.

A pale old warship, famous from the Battle of Trafalgar, is towed by a small steam tugboat to be broken up for scrap, while the sun sets in a blaze of gold. Turner showed the end of the age of sail and the start of the steam age. It was voted Britain's favorite painting in a 2005 poll. People still love its feeling of farewell.

Women in summery white dresses stroll and gather flowers in a sunny garden. Monet painted it outdoors, even digging a trench so he could reach the top of the huge canvas. The way sunlight filters through the dresses was striking. It was rejected from the 1867 Salon but is now treasured.

Two women sit on a sandy shore in Tahiti, relaxed and thoughtful, painted in bold, flat colors. Gauguin left France to live in the South Pacific hoping to find an unspoiled way of life. The strong colors and simple shapes were different from European art. It inspired later artists to use color freely.

paintings.t: The Intervention of the Sabine Women
paintings.m: Department of Paintings of the Louvre
paintings.why: In the legend of ancient Rome, women rush between two armies to stop a battle between their fathers and their husbands. David painted it after the French Revolution as a message of peace and unity. The figures are posed like statues in a clear, bright light. It took him years to complete.

Two girls in pretty dresses lean over a piano, gently reading music together. Renoir painted several versions of this scene, and the French government bought one for the Musée du Luxembourg. The soft, glowing colors give it a feeling of warmth. It's a gentle portrait of music at home.

In the Bible, Judith saves her city by defeating an enemy general. Klimt shows her in a shimmering gold collar, with half-closed eyes and a mysterious expression. The glittering patterns are inspired by Egyptian and Byzantine art. It's famous for combining ancient legend with modern, golden style.

A woman sleeps stretched backward on a bed as a creepy little creature sits on her chest and a horse's head peeks through the curtain. Fuseli's painting was a sensation in London in 1782, because it so vividly shows what it's like to have a bad dream. It's an early classic of the horror genre. It has inspired countless artists.

A group of women relax by a stream, painted with soft, sculptural outlines. Renoir spent three years working on it, trying to copy the classic style of Italian masters he'd admired on a trip. Critics weren't sure, because he'd left Impressionism behind. It marks a turning point in his career.

In Greek legend, a young man named Hylas goes to fetch water and is enchanted by water nymphs who pull him into their pond. Waterhouse painted the water lilies and glowing faces with great skill. It was displayed in Manchester Art Gallery, which once removed it for a few days in 2018 to spark a conversation. It is still a favorite of fans of myth and magic.

Two laborers break stones on a roadside, one old and one young, with faces hidden from view. Courbet saw them at work and invited them to model. Painting poor workers life-size was considered shocking. The original was destroyed in 1945 during World War II, but copies show its impact.

paintings.m: Department of Paintings of the Louvre
paintings.why: A woman sits on a bed seen from behind, her head wrapped in a turban, with silky white sheets and a curtain. Ingres painted this in Rome when he was just 28. Admirers praise the smooth, glowing skin and the elegant curve of her back. It's one of the best-known works of Neoclassical art.

A crowd of Parisians hurry along a rainy street under a sea of umbrellas. Renoir started this painting in his bright Impressionist style, then changed the figures on the left years later after he'd adopted a sharper, more classical look. That's why two styles live in one painting. It's a delightful picture of a rainy day in the city.

The goddess Venus drifts on the waves, her arm raised over her eyes, while little cupids fly around her. Cabanel's version was shown in 1863, the same year as Manet's scandalous picnic, and the Emperor Napoleon III bought it. It was the toast of the Paris Salon. It shows the polished, perfect style that Impressionists would rebel against.

Well-dressed Parisians stroll across a huge, wet intersection, holding umbrellas, with shiny gray cobblestones and handsome new buildings. Caillebotte painted it to show the modern, rebuilt Paris, which he knew well. The unusual cropping and perspective feel like a photograph. It's one of the best-known pictures of city life.

paintings.m: Kunst Museum Winterthur | Reinhart am Stadtgarten
paintings.why: Three people look out between tall white chalk cliffs and a twisted tree frame to the sparkling Baltic Sea. Friedrich painted it after his honeymoon on the island of Rügen, and the figures feel awestruck by the beauty. The hidden details, like the man on his hands and knees looking over the edge, invite you to imagine it yourself. It's among the most famous Romantic landscapes.

paintings.t: Agostina Segatori Sitting in the Café du Tambourin
paintings.why: A woman sits at a round table in a Paris café, her tambourine-shaped table, and cigarette at hand, in front of a wall covered with Japanese prints. Van Gogh knew her personally; she ran the café. He used bright, flat colors for the first time, after he moved to Paris. It's an early step toward his famous style.

An elderly man in colorful robes plays a flute, hoping to teach a group of tortoises. They creep along with little interest. Osman Hamdi Bey's painting is thought by many to be a gentle joke about how slowly people accept change. It's the most famous painting from Turkey and sold for a record price in 2004.

This tiny portrait, painted in watercolor on ivory, is about the size of a playing card. Sarah Goodridge was a miniature painter who made it in 1828 as a private gift to a friend. Because it is so small and personal, it's one of the most unusual works in early American art. It's remarkable for showing how a woman artist of the 1820s boldly made her own choices.

A stylish couple sits in a theater box, but the woman in her striped gown is looking out at the audience while the man peers up through binoculars. Renoir painted it in 1874 and showed it at the first Impressionist exhibition. It sparkles with black, white and pearly pink. It's loved for its elegance and its sense of being seen.

A young musician in a red-striped uniform stands against a plain light-gray background, playing his fife. Manet was inspired by Japanese prints and Velázquez in making the figure flat and bold. The Salon rejected it in 1866, and critics said it looked like a playing card. Today we cherish its simplicity and punch.

The ancient Roman emperor Heliogabalus is said to have thrown a party where guests were buried beneath a flood of rose petals. Alma-Tadema painted the shower of pink petals falling over the cheerful and doomed party. He studied roses so he could paint them in the correct season. It's celebrated for showing Rome as a world of luxury and drama.

Two girls in fancy hats and dresses sit on a terrace beside the Seine in Chatou, one holding a ball of wool. Renoir loved painting young people, and this one glows with soft red and green. It's also known as 'On the Terrace.' It was one of his big successes.

A tiny figure stands on a deserted beach before a huge, empty sea and stormy sky. Friedrich originally painted a few boats but covered them up, leaving only sea, sky, and a lone person. The emptiness felt shocking and modern; a German writer said it was like having your eyelids cut off! It's now seen as a masterpiece about being alone with nature.

In 1410 the armies of Poland and Lithuania defeated the Teutonic Knights in one of the largest battles of medieval Europe. Matejko painted it nearly as big as a wall, with hundreds of soldiers in a swirling clash. Poland was not an independent nation when he painted it, so the picture inspired national pride. It remains Poland's most famous painting.

A glowing moon shines over a calm river and a few small huts, with a path of silvery light across the water. Kuindzhi hid lamps behind his canvases when showing them to make the moonlight seem almost real. In 1880 crowds lined up in the dark to look at it. It's still known for its magic glow.

Young working-class men relax and bathe along the Seine, with factory chimneys in the distance. Seurat painted it in his careful, smooth style, and the stillness feels like time has stopped. It was his first big painting, and it was turned down by the Salon. It's now admired as a calm, quiet and modern masterpiece.

Van Gogh looks out with intense green-blue eyes against a background of swirling blue waves, wearing a blue coat. He painted several self-portraits, partly because he could not afford models. This one was made in 1889 after leaving hospital. It's one of the best-known self-portraits in the world.

paintings.t: The Meeting, or Bonjour, Monsieur Courbet!
paintings.why: Courbet, with a walking stick and pack, is greeted by his wealthy patron, who bows to him — and the artist stands tall in the sun. The painting is a joke and a statement: a painter who thinks highly of himself. It was shown with a funny title in 1855. It's an iconic portrait of artistic confidence.

A woman and a small girl in front of a iron fence, with clouds of steam rising behind them from a train in a station. Manet painted it near the Gare Saint-Lazare in Paris. Neither of the figures looks at the train, which was unusual for such a subject. It's a snapshot of modern life with steam and iron.

Delicate white and pink flowers branch out against a pale blue sky. Van Gogh painted it for his new nephew, named after him, born to his brother Theo in 1890. The branches are painted large, like in Japanese prints. It's one of his most tender and joyful paintings.

Two little girls light paper lanterns at dusk, surrounded by tall lilies and roses. Sargent painted for months, working only for a few minutes each evening when the light was right. The title comes from a popular song of the time. It's one of the most magical pictures of twilight.

A young landowner and his wife pose proudly in their own fields in Suffolk, England, as if showing off their land. Gainsborough painted this when he was only 21, and it features crops and sheep as well as the couple. It is one of the most famous English portraits. It's also a record of how people showed off their wealth.

In the Greek myth, a vain young man falls in love with his own reflection, while the nymph Echo watches heartbroken. Waterhouse painted the dreamy, mossy pool in lovely detail. It's the origin of the words 'narcissist' and 'echo.' The painting is celebrated for bringing myth to life.

A woman in a dark landscape raises her hands in grief. Wright of Derby painted this from a poem about a woman mourning her husband. The moonlit night and dramatic lighting make the scene feel eerie. It's a haunting example of the artist's skill with light.

A young woman with glowing skin lifts her arms as the morning sun rises behind her, with the pale light of day. Bouguereau often painted allegories, scenes that represent ideas — here, the beginning of the day. He was a master of smooth, polished surfaces. The painting delighted viewers at the Paris Salon.

Degas painted his aunt's family in Florence: a stern mother in black, a father with his back turned, and two girls. The stiff arrangement suggests the tension in the household. Degas was in his twenties, and this big portrait showed his incredible eye for character. It's now in the Musée d'Orsay.

A thin, tired man walks into a room — he's a returning exile, and his family stares in stunned surprise. Repin painted the faces so carefully that each one tells a story. The picture asks viewers to imagine what happens next. It's one of the best-loved Russian paintings.

A solitary figure sits on a rock at dawn, wrestling with a hard decision, as described in the Bible. Kramskoi painted Jesus as a tired, thoughtful man, not a glowing saint. The grey and blue colors set a quiet mood. It's regarded as one of the great Russian religious paintings.

In a poem by Tennyson, a lady who lives in a tower is cursed to never look out directly, but she does, and sails to Camelot in a boat. Waterhouse shows her drifting in her boat, with candles flickering out. It's one of the most popular paintings in the Tate Britain. People love its mix of beauty and sadness.

A man and woman pause in a field at dusk, heads bowed in prayer when the church bell rings. Millet said he was inspired by childhood memories of his grandmother stopping the farm work to pray. It sold for a huge price and became one of the most reproduced images in the world. It's a calm picture of ordinary devotion.

A court jester in red sits alone and gloomy at a party while his king dances in the background. Stańczyk was a real Polish jester known for his wisdom. News has just arrived of a lost city, and he is the only one who sees the danger. The painting shows that the person who jokes may also be the one who worries the most.

A fallen angel with a tormented expression sits alone on a rocky peak with his head in his hands. Cabanel painted it in 1847, inspired by Milton's poem Paradise Lost. The painting shows both beauty and sorrow. It's a classic of the French Academy.

paintings.t: Circe Offering the Cup to Ulysses
paintings.why: The enchantress Circe holds out a magic cup to Ulysses, hoping to turn him into an animal, as she did to his crew. A mirror behind her shows the hero, alert and holding his sword. Waterhouse painted rich fabrics and a hall of green. It's a thrilling moment from Homer's Odyssey.

A blind girl sits at the roadside with her sister after a rainstorm, a double rainbow in the sky — which she cannot see. Millais painted it from the real countryside near Winchelsea in England, with its glowing, wet colors. She feels the warm sun and touches the grass. The painting makes us think about everything we notice and everything we miss.

A young woman is being sold at an oriental slave market and is displayed to buyers. Gérôme painted many scenes of the Middle East that he imagined from travel, and this painting shows a cruel practice. Today the artwork is mainly valued as a record of how Europeans looked at the world, and for what it teaches about the injustice of slavery. It's studied as much for history as for art.

paintings.t: Napoleon I on his Imperial Throne
paintings.why: Napoleon sits like a god on a golden throne, with the crown of laurel leaves and a scepter, in a gleaming robe. Ingres painted him in 1806, imitating old religious pictures of Jupiter and of kings. The detail of the fabric, gold and fur is extraordinary. It's a spectacular example of power portraiture.

paintings.m: Musée des Beaux-Arts de la ville de Paris
paintings.why: Two women in fancy dresses rest in the grass beside a river, one lying down and one sitting up with a hat. Courbet painted real contemporary women, not goddesses, which angered the critics of 1857. The painting is bold in its color and sense of ordinary leisure. It's seen as a step toward Impressionism.

In an ancient Roman arena, a victorious gladiator awaits the crowd's verdict — thumbs down, which meant show no mercy. Gérôme studied Roman history to get details right. The scene has inspired countless films about gladiators. It's one of the most famous images of ancient Rome.

A woman reclines on a red cushion, painted with warm colors and Modigliani's smooth, simplified shapes. It was shown in 1917, and the police closed the exhibition because of it. The painting later sold for more than $150 million in 2015. It's one of the most valuable paintings of the 20th century.

Only the head of a small dog peeks out at the bottom of a huge empty golden-brown space. Goya painted it on a wall of his house when he was an old man. Nobody knows what he meant, so people have been wondering ever since. Many see it as a quiet, powerful picture of feeling small and alone.

A woman in a corset and petticoat is at her mirror, powdering her face as a gentleman in a top hat waits on a sofa. Manet painted this just before Émile Zola's novel of the same name was published. The Salon of 1877 rejected it. It is a bold picture of Parisian life, with a bright, glowing white and blue palette.

A simple wooden chair with a pipe and tobacco sits on a tiled floor. Van Gogh painted it as a companion to a picture of Gauguin's much fancier chair. The ordinary chair in sunlight stands for the artist himself. It's one of the most famous portraits of a person who isn't there.

paintings.t: Christ in the House of His Parents
paintings.why: A young Jesus in a carpenter's workshop has hurt his hand on a nail, and his family gathers around him. Millais painted every shaving, tool and detail with scientific care, and the scene hints at future events. When it was shown in 1850, some critics, including Charles Dickens, hated it. Now it's treasured as a daring early Pre-Raphaelite painting.

paintings.m: Department of Paintings of the Louvre
paintings.why: Women relax in a richly decorated room in Algiers, with patterned fabrics and soft light. Delacroix visited North Africa in 1832 and made quick sketches, then painted this from memory. The bold colors and dazzling light influenced later artists like Renoir, Matisse and Picasso. It's a landmark of color.

Five figures stand on a beach at sunset as five ships sail along the horizon. They stand for different stages of life, from a child to an old man. Friedrich painted this late in his life. Its quiet mood makes people think about the passing of time.

paintings.t: The Emperor Napoleon in His Study at the Tuileries
paintings.why: Napoleon stands in his study at night in his general's uniform, his candles nearly burnt down and the clock showing about 4 a.m. David wanted to show him as a leader who works through the night for his people. The details, like the sword and the folded paper, were carefully chosen. It's among the most famous portraits of Napoleon.

paintings.t: Romeo and Juliet: the Tomb Scene
paintings.why: Romeo has taken poison, and Juliet is waking up in the crypt, with a lamp casting a dramatic glow. Wright of Derby painted several scenes from Shakespeare's plays. His use of dark and light heightens the tragedy. It's a moving take on one of the greatest love stories.

A young woman in a straw hat leans against a tree, wrapped in a warm, hazy summer light. Renoir painted this when he was 27, still finding his style. The modeled flesh and dappled leaves are a early taste of his later work. It's a pleasant picture of summer relaxation.

Breton women in white caps imagine a scene from the Bible — Jacob wrestling an angel — after hearing a sermon. Gauguin painted the vision with a solid red field and no realistic depth, to show it's a dream. The tree slices across the canvas like a Japanese print. It's a key early work of modern, symbolic art.

Three men kneel on the floor of an apartment to scrape and plane a wooden floor, their bare backs gleaming. Caillebotte painted the workers with the same care as a rich family. This was rare and a bit shocking in 1875. It's famous for its dramatic perspective and its respect for labor.

A circus rider leaps off a galloping white horse, a ringmaster cracks his whip and a clown tumbles. Seurat's last painting is made of tiny dots, with swirling lines to suggest motion. He died before he finished it, in 1891. It remains a lively picture of a night out.

A white-bearded figure leans out of a glowing orb in the sky, stretching down a giant pair of compasses to measure and create the world. Blake made this as a print and painted it by hand, and he reportedly worked on it near the end of his life. It shows God as a great designer, but also a bit scary. It's one of the most famous images of creation in art.

A girl sits at a table in a sunny dining room, peaches and a knife in front of her and light dancing on her face. Serov painted twelve-year-old Vera Mamontova at her family's country home, working for weeks on the portrait. The fresh, natural light was a joy after stiff, formal portraits. It's one of Russia's best-loved paintings.

A woman kneels to sift grain in a barn while her brother and a younger sibling work beside her. Courbet painted ordinary farm work in warm golden tones, in a large canvas that usually would have been reserved for gods. It was part of his movement to paint real life. It shows the dignity of everyday jobs.

In ancient Greece, the clever lawyer Hypereides defended the famous Phryne in a court. To win the case, he dramatically revealed her to the judges, who were so struck that they let her go. Gérôme made this a scene of high drama. It's remembered as a study of beauty and justice.

A magpie perches on a gate in a quiet field of dazzling snow, with a small house in the background. Monet painted the shadows in blues and lilacs instead of gray, which was radical in 1869. It's one of the loveliest snow scenes in art. The tiny black-and-white bird gives it humor and rhythm.

A young Tahitian girl lies on a bed, looking back with fear, while a ghostly figure watches from behind. The title means 'the spirit of the dead is watching.' Gauguin painted it in Tahiti, mixing local beliefs with his own imagination. The bold, flat color helped inspire later modern art.

A young girl in a rough dress stands in a field with sheep in the background, gazing directly out. Bouguereau often painted peasant children in soft light. His technique makes the skin glow and the fabrics look real. The painting was popular with collectors in America and Europe.

A group of people gather around a violinist in a poor quarter of Paris, including children and a man in a top hat. Manet borrowed figures from old master paintings to tell a modern tale. The painting is about poor people on the edges of society, treated with respect. It's an early work showing his big ambitions.

paintings.m: National Museum of Fine Arts, Argentina
paintings.why: In the Bible, Adam and Eve are overcome with grief over their son Abel, who has died at the hand of his brother Cain. Bouguereau's painting is moving because of the tenderness of the mother cradling her son. It was done with the smooth, polished style he was famous for. It makes the first sadness in human history feel real.
l: National Museum of Fine Arts, Argentina

paintings.why: A young woman in a flowing white summer dress stands in a sunny garden with her parasol and fresh flowers. Monet painted it in 1867, with strong contrast between light and shadow. Some experts think it was painted from the same model as 'Women in the Garden'. It's an early example of Impressionist sunshine.

A young woman in a white dress stands beneath a shady parasol, with sunlight sneaking in through the leaves. The model was Lise Tréhot, Renoir's girlfriend and favorite model. The Salon accepted it in 1868, and it was a hit. The dappled light is a hint of Renoir's later Impressionism.

paintings.t: Berthe Morisot with a Bouquet of Violets
paintings.why: A woman in black with large, dark eyes looks out, a small bunch of violets pinned to her dress. Berthe Morisot was a painter herself and Manet's friend. This is one of the most compelling portraits of an artist by another. She later married Manet's brother.

Prisoners walk in a circle in a high-walled courtyard, with no way out. Van Gogh painted this in an asylum in 1890, copying an illustration by Gustave Doré. Many viewers feel he was thinking of his own confinement. The painting is a deep expression of being trapped.

A smiling woman in a pink dress and straw hat twirls with a man in a straw boater, in a crowd of happy dancers. Renoir's wife Aline, who was his model, appears in one of the dance scenes. He painted it as a companion to the city dance scene. It's a joyous moment.

A tiger crouches amid lashing leaves, rain and lightning, hunting its prey. Rousseau's first jungle painting wasn't based on a real jungle trip but on books and plant gardens. The result is fantastically vivid. It made the art world see his 'naive' style as magical.

paintings.t: Symphony in White, No. 1: The White Girl
paintings.why: A young woman in a long white dress stands on a white fur rug against a white curtain. Whistler wanted a painting of harmony in color, like music. The model was Joanna Hiffernan, his partner. It was rejected from the Salon but exhibited at the 'Salon of the Rejected.'

A couple and their baby, huddled under a big umbrella, look out at the sea as they emigrate, leaving England behind. Brown based it on a friend who was leaving for Australia. The colors are painted outdoors in raw daylight, in a round frame. It's an emotional picture about leaving home.

Guests of the famous Paris nightclub gather around a table, with a woman in the foreground lit with a ghostly green face. Toulouse-Lautrec was a regular there and painted the real people he knew. He flattened the space and used strong color. It's one of the most famous images of Paris nightlife.

A man in a dark suit sweeps a woman in a long white ballgown across the dance floor, tropical plants behind them. Renoir painted this as a companion to his country dance painting, contrasting the formal and the casual. The woman is Suzanne Valadon, who became a famous painter. It's a chic image of city life.

paintings.t: The Execution of Lady Jane Grey
paintings.why: A blindfolded young queen feels for the block as she is about to be beheaded. Jane Grey was queen of England for nine days in 1553 and was only a teenager. Delaroche painted the moment with a hush that makes it moving. When it was shown in 1834, crowds were moved to tears.

A wealthy lady in a pale flowered dress sits with an amazing calm gaze, in a gleaming gilt room. Ingres painted her twice; this is the seated one, with her chin on her hand. He labored for years to get the textures of silk and jewels perfect. It's one of the greatest portraits of the 1800s.

paintings.t: Greece on the Ruins of Missolonghi
paintings.why: A woman, a symbol of Greece, stretches out her arms among ruins after a terrible siege during the Greek War of Independence. Delacroix painted it to raise money for the Greek cause. It's a cry for help made in paint. It shows how art can speak about real events.

A mother or nurse gently bathes a little girl's feet in a basin, seen from high above. Cassatt was influenced by Japanese prints and used simple shapes and bold lines. The tender moment between the two is full of warmth. It's among the most famous works by an American Impressionist.

paintings.m: Department of Paintings of the Louvre
paintings.why: The goddess Diana rests after her bath, with a servant tending to her feet and hunting gear scattered around. Boucher painted soft pink skin and silky fabric, in the playful French Rococo style. It is full of charm and decorative detail. It was owned by the French king's circle.

A woman wraps her red hair and arms around a man, her head against his neck. Munch called it 'Love and Pain' at first. Other people thought it looked like a vampire, so the name stuck. It is one of his best-known works about the complexity of love.

A young woman with red hair and a black dress sits sideways, looking out in a thoughtful way. Schiele painted his model Wally Neuzil, who lived with him in Vienna. After World War II, the painting was involved in a long legal fight about stolen art. It ended in 2010.

Jesus stands at night in a garden with a lantern, knocking at an overgrown door that has no handle on the outside. Hunt painted it to show that you must open your heart from the inside. It toured the world and was seen by millions. It's one of the most reproduced religious paintings ever.

A young woman with a long neck, tilted head and almond-shaped eyes sits in a simple blue-and-black dress. Modigliani painted this in 1918, near the end of his short life. The elongated style is his signature. It is a graceful example of his gentle, calm portraits.

paintings.m: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea di Roma
paintings.why: A baby, a young mother and an old woman appear together in Klimt's gold-and-pattern style. The painting shows the cycle of life. It won a gold medal at an exhibition in Rome. The old woman at the side shows Klimt's honest view of aging.
l: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea di Roma

paintings.why: A brooding, sad winged demon sits in a mountain landscape, with eyes full of longing. Vrubel was inspired by a poem by Lermontov. The faceted, mosaic-like paint looks like jewels. It became a great symbol of Russian art.

In the legend of King Arthur, the wizard Merlin is tricked by the enchantress Nimue into a trance. Burne-Jones painted the pair among a dark and tangled forest. The rich colors and details are like a medieval tapestry. It's a prime example of Victorian fantasy art.

A giant goat stands in the dark in front of a crowd of witches with sallow faces. Goya painted it on his wall in his 70s. It may be about fear and superstition. It's among his strange, shadowy 'Black Paintings.'

paintings.t: Truth Coming Out of Her Well
paintings.why: The figure of Truth emerges from a well, holding a whip to punish liars. Gérôme painted this near the end of his life as a response to critics who disliked him. It's allegory, a picture in which a person stands for an idea. It's a funny and bold painting.

A young woman in a flowery hat and a fresh dress stands in a garden of green. Manet painted it near the end of his life when he was ill. The model, actress Jeanne Demarsy, represents the season. It's a happy picture of renewal.

Van Gogh's face looks intense and slightly orange against swirling blue-green strokes. This is one of his last self-portraits, painted in 1889. It's one of the only paintings he made without a beard. It sold for a record price in 1998.

A dark and empty ocean stretches to the horizon, with strange curls of cloud and one small ray of sun. Watts painted it as the end of the great Flood from the Bible, with no people in sight. It's a mysterious picture of nature before humans. It looks almost modern.

A woman in a bold pattern of red and gold looks out with a graceful pose, holding a fan. It was one of Klimt's last portraits, painted in 1917, shortly before his death. It was rediscovered in 2023 and sold for around $85 million. Its bright palette and decoration show his later style.

paintings.m: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design
paintings.why: A wedding party rows a boat full of people in traditional costume across a fjord, with mountains behind them. Tidemand painted the figures and Gude painted the landscape — a team effort. It became an icon of Norwegian identity. It's famous for making the country's culture proud.
l: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design

paintings.why: A slightly tilted white square floats on a white background. Malevich wanted to make pictures with no objects, only pure feeling. It's one of the most radical paintings ever created. People still discuss what it means and whether it's art.

Two men stand under twisted oak trees and gaze at the glowing crescent moon in the evening sky. Friedrich painted himself and a student or friend. The scene is quiet and thoughtful. It's a favorite Romantic image of friendship and wonder.

paintings.t: Salisbury Cathedral from the Bishop's Grounds
paintings.m: Victoria and Albert museum prints, drawings, & paintings collection
paintings.why: The spire of the cathedral rises into a stormy sky, framed by a dark arch of trees. Constable painted it for his friend the Bishop of Salisbury. There's a rainbow, which he used to show hope. It's a masterpiece of English landscape painting.

A great valley in Ecuador, with waterfalls, mountain peaks, tiny villagers and tropical plants. Church painted this huge canvas after trips to South America. In 1859 New Yorkers paid to see it, and crowds used binoculars to look at details. It made him famous.

paintings.t: Nocturne in Black and Gold – The Falling Rocket
paintings.why: Fireworks fizzle in a dark sky above a London park. Whistler painted it with a few dabs, and the critic John Ruskin said he was 'flinging a pot of paint in the public's face.' Whistler sued him for libel and won a farthing in damages. It started a famous argument about what art should be.

A woman sits in a Paris café, a plum on the table in front of her, deep in thought. Manet painted it in the last years of his life. The painting is about waiting and thinking. It's famous for capturing a mood.

paintings.m: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium
paintings.why: The god of war, Mars, is gently disarmed by Venus, goddess of love, as cupids remove his weapons. David painted it at the end of his career, when he was in exile in Brussels. The message, 'make love, not war', feels timeless. It's grand and calm in style.
l: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium

paintings.m: Amon Carter Museum of American Art
paintings.why: Young men relax and swim from a wooden platform at a pond. Eakins painted friends and students, and himself swimming in the water at the right. He was also a talented photographer and used it to study movement. It's a famous picture of American life.
l: Amon Carter Museum of American Art

paintings.why: A woman with closed eyes sits with her head tilted back, while a bird drops a poppy into her hands. Rossetti painted it after the death of his wife Elizabeth Siddal. The figure is Beatrice from Dante's poems. It's a picture of love and grief.

Three models in a studio, shown in front, back and side views, with Seurat's own giant painting behind them. He used dots of color to prove that his method works for indoor scenes. The picture is partly a response to critics. It's a clever, calm and quiet painting.

A young Japanese girl sits on a chair, with a flower in her hand, in a patterned jacket and a green and orange background. Van Gogh was obsessed with Japanese art, though he had never been to Japan. The word 'mousmé' was something he learned from a novel. It's a vibrant, joyful portrait.

A woman holds a pomegranate, with a dark and sorrowful gaze. In the Roman myth, Proserpine ate pomegranate seeds in the underworld and was forced to return for part of each year. Rossetti's muse Jane Morris was the model. It's a symbol of winter and longing.

Monet planned this huge picnic scene as a challenge to Manet's famous painting of the same name, but this time with well-dressed friends in the forest. He worked on it outdoors in 1865–66, then left it unfinished and later cut it up; only pieces and the sketch survive. Dappled sunlight on the tablecloth made it a ground-breaking study of light. It shows how ambitious the young Impressionists were.

paintings.m: Department of Paintings of the Louvre
paintings.why: A young girl sits alone in a graveyard, eyes wide and shoulders hunched, her face lit by a pale light. Delacroix painted it as a study for a larger work about misery and suffering. The fear and sadness in her large dark eyes feel startlingly real. It's one of the great emotional portraits of Romanticism.

Five men present a document to a room full of delegates in Philadelphia in 1776. Trumbull, who had served in the Revolution, painted it with portraits from life, hoping to get faces right. It's the image of the Declaration signing that many Americans know, and it appears on the two-dollar bill. It hangs in the U.S. Capitol Rotunda today.

paintings.m: San Francisco Museum of Modern Art
paintings.why: A woman in a feathered hat and dress is painted with wild green, orange and purple stripes across her face. When Matisse showed it in 1905, critics were shocked and called the group 'les fauves' — 'the wild beasts.' He wanted color to express feelings, not match reality. It changed how modern artists thought about color.
l: San Francisco Museum of Modern Art

paintings.why: A group of young women float in a swirl of colorful patterns and flowers, as if dreaming. Klimt painted this when he was 51, using bright reds, blues and golds. The figures seem to melt into one another and into the decoration. It's famous for its dazzling rhythm.

A huge pile of skulls stands in a barren desert, with crows circling above. Vereshchagin dedicated it 'to all conquerors, past, present and future.' He had seen war himself and wanted to show its cost. It's one of the most famous anti-war paintings.

A family walks together in the countryside in warm, glowing sunlight. Sorolla was a master at painting light, especially bright, sunny scenes. His mix of loose brushwork and joyful mood made him famous in Spain and beyond. He painted it in Spain in 1909.

A huge crowd of people, rich and poor, follow a sacred icon down a dusty road under a hot sun. Repin painted hundreds of figures, and each one has a different face and story. The painting took him years, and he traveled to villages for sketches. It's a panorama of 19th-century Russia.

Red poppies and blue cornflowers burst from a vase in a bright burst of color. Van Gogh painted this when he lived in Paris, discovering brighter colors from his Impressionist friends. The lively brushstrokes fill the canvas. In 2010, it was stolen from a museum in Cairo, and it's still missing.
l: Stolen from the Mohamed Mahmoud Khalil Museum in Cairo in 2010 and still missing

paintings.why: Crowds stream down the steps of Warsaw's Royal Castle to celebrate the first modern written constitution in Europe. Matejko painted it to remind Poles of their proud past when Poland was ruled by foreign powers. People throng the stairs and cheer. It's a symbol of hope and freedom for Poland.

paintings.m: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium
paintings.why: A green Christ on the cross is shown in a Breton landscape, as women in traditional caps mourn. Gauguin used flat, symbolic color, in contrast to realistic painting. It's also called 'The Breton Calvary.' It's a key example of his style, known as Synthetism.
l: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium

paintings.why: The writer Émile Zola sits at his desk surrounded by objects that tell us about him: a pamphlet by Manet's supporter, a Japanese print and an image of Olympia. Zola had defended Manet in print when critics attacked him. Manet painted this as a thank you. It's a portrait of friendship.

A couple twirl across a café terrace — the man in a straw boater and the woman in a red-trimmed dress and hat. Renoir's model was Suzanne Valadon, who became a famous painter herself. The painting is full of energy, and her flushed cheeks are lifelike. It's one of the best-known dance paintings.

A simple red rectangle tilts on a white background. Malevich called it 'a peasant woman in two dimensions.' It was part of his radical art movement, Suprematism. It's a milestone in the story of abstract art.

A woman in a shawl and dress sits with a basket of oranges on her lap, selling fruit in Warsaw. Gierymski painted her with great care and sympathy. It was a rare picture that gave a poor street vendor the dignity of a portrait. It's one of the most beloved Polish paintings.

Huge powerful horses rear and parade at a horse market in Paris, held by their handlers. Bonheur sketched at the market for 18 months, even dressing in men's clothes to blend in. The painting is more than 5 meters wide. It made her an international star and the greatest animal painter of her day.

A rainbow glows over a misty mountain valley, with a cross on a rock. Friedrich painted nature as something sacred. The soft, delicate light makes it feel peaceful. It's an early example of his Romantic style.

paintings.t: The Daughters of Edward Darley Boit
paintings.why: Four sisters pose in a tall, dark entry hall with huge Japanese vases — one on the floor, others standing in shadow. Sargent painted them at different distances, so the room feels deep and strange. Some people see it as a mysterious, dreamlike picture. It's one of the most famous American portraits.

A young woman in a pink dress sits with her back turned, gazing at a village on a sunlit hill in southern France. Bazille painted it for his family, using bold light in the open air. The style looks forward to Impressionism. It's among his most famous works.

A young woman is nervously kissed by a lover, while a secret meeting is happening in a room full of beautiful satin. Fragonard and Gérard worked together on this scene of intrigue. The shiny dress is dazzling. It's a classic 18th-century romantic painting.

Napoleon, still a young general, sits on his horse before the Great Sphinx in Egypt. Gérôme painted the face of the Sphinx as if the two are staring at each other. The scene has a mysterious, silent feel. It's a famous image of the clash of old and new.

paintings.t: Bonaparte Visiting the Plague Victims of Jaffa
paintings.m: Department of Paintings of the Louvre
paintings.why: Napoleon reaches out to touch a sick soldier during a plague outbreak in 1799, as others reel in fear. Gros painted it to show a brave leader, though the story is partly propaganda. The exotic setting with its arches and light is dramatic. It's a turning point from Neoclassical to Romantic painting.

paintings.m: Department of Paintings of the Louvre
paintings.why: A heavy-set man sits with his hands on his knees and a powerful gaze. Louis-François Bertin was the editor of a major newspaper, and Ingres captured his strong personality. When it was shown in 1833, it was admired as an image of the rising middle class. Edgar Degas later called it the portrait of the new age.

People in rowing boats and bathers fill a floating café in a bend of the Seine near Paris. Monet and Renoir painted side by side at this popular spot in 1869, inventing the Impressionist style. The water is painted with dabs of light and color. It's a landmark in art history.

paintings.t: The Dessert: Harmony in Red (The Red Room)
paintings.why: A woman arranges fruit and wine on a table in a room where everything is red: the walls and the tablecloth blend, patterned with blue vines. Matisse first painted it in blue and then changed it to red. The flat patterns and strong color changed how artists treat space. It's a landmark of modern art.

The goddess Venus rises from the sea, wringing out her hair, as little cupids flutter around her. Ingres began this painting in the 1800s, and he finished it in 1848, in his sixties. It's a picture of a classic myth in a smooth, graceful style. It still hangs in a museum in Chantilly, France.

A man in a long black cape and top hat stands by a wall with an empty bottle beside him. Manet painted a ragpicker of Paris as if he were a noble. The Salon rejected it in 1859. It was his first major painting and shows an early sympathy for ordinary people.

paintings.m: Musée des Beaux-Arts et d'Archéologie de Besançon
paintings.why: A hunter pulls a deer from a stream in a snowy forest, with a hunting horn and hound beside him. Courbet loved his native forest and painted many hunt scenes. The dark, rich shadows and glittering water show his skill. It's a bold, realistic image of country life.
l: Musée des Beaux-Arts et d'Archéologie de Besançon

paintings.t: Self-Portrait with Death Playing the Fiddle
paintings.why: The painter pauses at his easel, as a skeleton with a one-stringed fiddle whispers in his ear. Böcklin painted this as a reminder that life is short and art is precious. The skeleton is slightly funny and slightly spooky. It's an important painting of Symbolism.

A young man sits against a tree, half-conscious, with a sword by his side and blood on his shirt. Courbet painted himself in this dramatic role when he was 25. He changed the painting years later, removing a woman who was originally beside him. It's an early picture showing his ambition.

A young man falls into Havana harbor while swimming and is attacked by a shark, and sailors desperately try to rescue him. Brook Watson, the real victim, lost a leg but later became Lord Mayor of London. Copley painted the tense moment with dramatic action. It's a thrilling, true-life adventure.

A girl with long red hair and bright blue eyes sits in a luxurious blue-and-white dress. Renoir painted her when she was eight, the daughter of a rich banker. Her family wasn't pleased with the picture and hung it in a back hall. Today it's treasured as one of his best portraits.

Van Gogh sits at his easel, painting a vase of sunflowers, while Gauguin watches closely. Gauguin painted this picture when they lived together in Arles. Van Gogh said it looked like him, 'but gone mad.' It's a rare picture of one great artist painting another.

A man in a Spanish costume sits on a bench, strumming a guitar, with his legs crossed. Manet's first big success, shown in the 1861 Salon, with strong light and dark. Critics admired its life-like quality. It's among his best works from the early period.

A man in black glides across an icy pond on one leg, arms crossed, wearing a black hat. Reverend Robert Walker was a member of a skating club in Edinburgh. Raeburn painted him in a lively pose, which made the portrait famous. It is one of the most popular paintings in Scotland.

A man and woman stroll in a sunlit wooded park, followed by a child, light dappled across her pale dress. Renoir painted this in 1870, before the Franco-Prussian War. It's an early example of his love of sunlit scenes. It reveals his talent for capturing a happy moment.

paintings.m: Department of Paintings of the Louvre
paintings.why: A woman in a simple white gown reclines on a long Greek-style sofa in an empty room. David left it unfinished, and Madame Récamier was so annoyed that she hired another artist. The simple lines and clean look are ahead of their time. It's one of the most famous portraits of the 1800s.

A gigantic figure rises behind a mountain in the dusk as the tiny people below flee in fear. Goya's inspiration may be war or fear. Because experts now question whether he painted it, it's still a mystery. It's one of the most mysterious images in art.

paintings.t: Memory of the Garden at Etten
paintings.why: Two women stroll in a garden of dahlias and flowers, remembering the garden where Van Gogh's family lived in the Netherlands. He painted it from memory in Arles, thinking of his mother and sister. The colors are bold and dreamlike. It's a tender family memory.

Twisted roots and trunks spread across a forest bank, painted in swirling green, yellow and brown. It's thought to be the last painting Van Gogh made, in July 1890. The roots look alive, as if reaching for something. It's one of his most vivid late works.

Nude figures lounge, dance and play music in a meadow in bright, wild colors. Matisse painted it as a vision of a golden age, a paradise. The flat shapes and flowing lines were revolutionary. It changed the course of modern art.

paintings.t: Astronomer Copernicus, or Conversations with God
paintings.why: A scholar stands on a balcony at night with a telescope and instruments, gazing at the sky. Matejko painted Nicolaus Copernicus, who showed that the Earth goes around the Sun. The painting celebrates a Polish genius. It's a tribute to curiosity and bold ideas.

paintings.t: The Appearance of Christ Before the People
paintings.why: A crowd in the Roman Empire gathers by a river to hear John the Baptist, as Jesus approaches in the distance. Alexander Ivanov spent about 20 years painting it in Rome. He studied people from all backgrounds. It's one of Russia's most important religious paintings.

A young woman sits beside a mountain stream in a forest, with the cool, clear water flowing around her. Courbet painted her as a real person instead of an idealized goddess. The forest and water glisten. It's a rare nature scene painted with the same care as a portrait.

An elderly woman sits with her hands folded in a dark dress. Van Gogh painted it in 1888 from a black-and-white photograph. He used bold greens and reds to make it more alive. It's an affectionate portrait of the mother he loved.

Bathers splash in the water near a floating café on the Seine, painted with quick, sparkling dabs of paint. Renoir and Monet worked side by side here in 1869, and both made paintings of it. The water is painted in lively color. It's one of the first Impressionist paintings.

A skeleton in a dark robe stands beside a heap of people of all ages, wrapped up in dazzling, colorful patterns. Klimt painted the circle of life, with Death and the living side by side. It won a prize in Rome and Klimt later repainted it. It's a thoughtful picture about life's cycle.

A group of Scandinavian artists in Rome gather in a tavern, laughing, drinking and playing music. Bloch lived in Rome as a student and painted his friends. It's lively and warm. It shows what the lives of young artists were like.

An architect lies on a giant column, dreaming of a huge city of classical buildings from all over the world. Cole painted it for an architect friend. It's a fantasy of great architecture. It's one of the most imaginative American paintings of its time.

A woman reclines on a couch in the middle of a lush jungle, surrounded by lions, birds, snakes and a flute player in the moonlight. Rousseau said she was dreaming the whole scene. He painted it in his last year, in an amazing, flat style, with every leaf carefully shaped. It's one of the world's most famous dreamlike paintings.

A ship sails off into a fiery red sunset on a stormy sea, while in the foreground chains and the legs of drowning people float in the waves. Turner was inspired by a true story, in which enslaved people were thrown overboard. He used blazing colors to make people feel the horror of the slave trade. It's a powerful reminder that art can speak out against cruelty.

Sailboats with white sails and flags dot a bright blue sea, as spectators in small boats watch the races. Monet painted the Normandy coast in simple blocks of bright color. The flat shapes show the influence of Japanese prints. It's a cheerful picture of a summer day by the sea.

A family sits at a long dinner table, and the two lovers, Isabella and Lorenzo, are at the center, their feelings hidden. Millais based it on a poem by Keats, and he used his friends and family as models. He painted every detail with great sharpness, which was a daring approach in 1849. It marks the beginning of the Pre-Raphaelite movement.

A young man tears at his hair, his eyes wide, staring straight at us. Courbet painted himself in an exaggerated expression of shock and fear, perhaps acting like a character on a stage. It was his early way to show he could paint strong emotions. It has become one of his best-known self-portraits.

A woman's face is split by a vibrant green stripe down the nose, set against pink, orange and purple backgrounds. Matisse painted his wife Amélie in 1905, using color instead of ordinary shadows. Critics were baffled, but he said color could build a picture. It's a classic Fauvist work.

A young girl stands with her arms around herself at the edge of a morning lake, in soft hazy light. Chabas painted it in 1912, and it became so famous that millions of copies were sold. A famous controversy in the U.S. made it even more popular. It's a great example of how a painting can become a pop-culture sensation.

A little boy in a bright red suit holds a string tied to a pet magpie, while three cats watch with wide, hungry eyes. Goya painted him as a small child of a noble family. The cats lurk in the shadows, a hint at danger. It's among the most charming and beloved portraits of a child.

paintings.m: National Museum of Fine Arts, Argentina
paintings.why: A nymph, startled in a woodland pool, looks out at someone who has surprised her. Manet painted it as a young man, studying the old masters. It's an unusual painting in his early style. It shows how he began by learning from the past.
l: National Museum of Fine Arts, Argentina

paintings.why: Queen Dido oversees the building of the city of Carthage by a glittering harbor in the golden light of sunrise. Turner was inspired by the paintings of Claude Lorrain, whom he admired. He wanted his work hung next to Claude's, and it still hangs there in the National Gallery. It is among the most beautiful sunrises in art.

A Tahitian woman carries a child on her shoulder, with a glowing halo, as the angel greets them. The title means 'Hail Mary' in the Tahitian language. Gauguin blended Christian images with island life. It's a bright and unusual Nativity.

A cross rises on a mountaintop, surrounded by evergreen trees and glowing light. Friedrich painted it as an altarpiece, but it was more of a landscape than a typical religious painting, which caused a huge argument. It showed that nature could be a way to feel God. It was one of the most debated paintings of its time.

A tall Pierrot and a Harlequin in costume stride arm in arm in a carnival masquerade. Cézanne's son Paul and a friend posed for it. The stiff, theater-like figures make a lively picture. It shows how Cézanne painted with simple shapes and blocks of color.
A teenage girl with a baby on her lap smiles in a green meadow. Bouguereau's soft-focus style was widely loved. The baby plays with her hair. It's a tender picture of family.

paintings.t: Portrait of a Lady in Blue
paintings.why: A woman in a shimmering blue gown, with a feathery hat, looks out at us with a gentle smile. Gainsborough painted with fluttery strokes that make the silk glow. We don't know who she is, but she has captured the world's attention. It is one of the best-loved portraits of the 18th century.

paintings.t: Erasistratus Discovering the Cause of Antiochus' Disease
paintings.why: A doctor figures out that a prince is sick with love, as the prince's stepmother stands nearby. David painted it to win the Prix de Rome, the top art prize in France, in 1774. The clear composition and strong emotions won him the prize. It launched his career.

paintings.t: Portrait of Doña Isabel de Porcel
paintings.why: A confident woman in black lace stands with her hands on her hips, framed by a dark background. Goya painted this in 1805. The portrait is wonderfully direct and strong. It's one of the finest of his female portraits.

Women lie and sit in the sun on a Tahitian beach, with the sea behind. The title means 'What! Are you jealous?' Gauguin used flat areas of strong color. The picture is a colorful reflection of island life.

A line of soldiers who have been blinded by poison gas each rest a hand on the shoulder of the man ahead, walking toward a medical station. Sargent saw this scene for real in 1918 during World War I. The painting is enormous, nearly seven meters wide. It's one of the most memorable pictures of the war.
A woman sits reading in a quiet room, painted in warm yellows and browns. It is an early work by Matisse, painted before his famous wild colors. It's a calm moment of quiet concentration.

paintings.m: Department of Paintings of the Louvre
paintings.why: A young man faces a monster with a woman's head and a lion's body, who asks riddles of travelers. In the Greek legend, Oedipus solved the riddle and saved the city of Thebes. Ingres painted it as a student in Rome. It's a young artist's tribute to classical stories.

paintings.t: Portrait of the actress Jeanne Samary
paintings.why: A smiling young woman in a gown of white and rose holds a smile that seems about to turn into a laugh. Jeanne Samary was a Comédie-Française actress and a friend of Renoir. His colors dance across the dress and the background. It's a lovely, lively portrait.

A woman in a dress sits on a donkey, with a patch of light on her face, riding to market in Bordeaux. Goya painted this in exile near the end of his life, at age 80. The loose brushstrokes made him a forerunner of the Impressionists. It shows his youthful spirit even in old age.

A tree with red-orange limbs twists against a blue background. Mondrian painted this early in his career, using color instead of realism. Later he would simplify trees into lines and grids. It's an important step on his journey to abstract art.

Two cherubic children stand cheek to cheek, Cupid with wings and Psyche, holding a butterfly. Bouguereau retold a Roman myth of love in his sweet, polished style. It was extremely popular with collectors. It's an enchanting picture.

A sorceress leans over a pool, pouring poison into the water to turn her rival into a sea monster. Waterhouse captured the magic glowing in the water. Her swirling green robes are painted in vivid colors. It's a story from Greek mythology made vivid.

Four girls in an orchard at twilight burn piles of fallen leaves, with a glowing red sky behind. Millais painted the smoky sunset after a quiet autumn evening in Scotland. The painting is about the passing of seasons and of time. It's known for its subtle glow.

paintings.t: Harvest at La Crau, with Montmajour in the Background
paintings.why: A golden wheat field stretches across the plain under a blue sky, with farmers and wagons working in the sun. Van Gogh painted it in just a few days in June 1888, in the heat of the south of France. The colors are those of his beloved Provence. It's a bright celebration of harvest.

paintings.t: The Lictors Bring to Brutus the Bodies of His Sons
paintings.m: Department of Paintings of the Louvre
paintings.why: A Roman leader sits in the shadows, brooding, as his sons' bodies are carried in because he condemned them for treason. His wife and daughters are in anguish. David showed the hard cost of duty. It was exhibited in 1789 as the French Revolution began.

A small figure walks across a snowy field with a fence, with a peaceful purple-blue wash of color beyond. Van Gogh was fascinated by the winter in Arles. The painting uses crisp, simple lines like a Japanese print. It's a calm scene.

A blindfolded woman sits on a globe, playing a lyre with one string left. In the dim, starry sky a single star shines. Watts painted this as a message about holding on to hope in hard times. It inspired later leaders, and a famous 2004 speech used its title.

paintings.t: Morning of the Execution of the Streltsy
paintings.why: On Red Square in Moscow in 1698, Peter the Great watches as rebel soldiers, the Streltsy, are about to be executed. Surikov painted the crowds in a clash of faces and colors. The tension makes you feel as if you're in the crowd. It is one of the great Russian history paintings.

Fields of tulips and bulbs make broad stripes of color across the flat Dutch landscape, with a village in the distance. Van Gogh painted this in 1883 in the Netherlands, when his palette was still dark. The pattern of stripes anticipates his bolder style. It's a bright patch of flowers.

A woman lies back on a bed in a quiet room, painted with soft light. Courbet was a Realist who painted real people, not fairy-tale goddesses. It shows his skill with textures and light. It's an example of his straightforward style.

A young woman lies in the snow with a white dove rising from her lips, as a group of people gather at the back. Saint Eulalia was a young Christian girl from Spain who was martyred, according to legend. Waterhouse painted her peaceful face as the dove symbolizes her spirit. It is a haunting picture of courage.

Waves of green wheat ripple around a tall cypress, against a swirling sky. Van Gogh painted it in the south of France at an asylum. Cypresses, to him, were as beautiful as Egyptian obelisks. It's a joyful, energetic image of nature.

A woman jumps up from her lover's lap in a fancy room, as if she suddenly realizes something. Hunt packed the painting with symbols, like a cat chasing a bird. He wanted to teach a moral lesson, in the Victorian way. It's famous for its fine detail.

A rolled-up carpet is unrolled at Julius Caesar's feet, and out peeks Cleopatra. The story says she was smuggled into his palace this way. Gérôme painted the moment of surprise in rich detail. It's a dramatic episode from ancient history.

Teams of strong white oxen pull ploughs through brown earth in central France. Bonheur spent time on farms, studying the animals. The painting was bought by the French government. It's a landmark in realistic animal painting.

paintings.t: Young Greeks Attending a Cock Fight
paintings.why: Young men and women in ancient Greece watch two roosters fighting. Gérôme's first big success at the Salon in 1847. He imagined the scene based on his studies of ancient Greece. The painting launched his career.

The hero Ulysses is tied to the mast of his ship so that he can listen to the sirens' song without crashing into rocks. His sailors have their ears plugged with wax. Etty painted the swirl of sea nymphs in a tangle of sea and sky. It's a retelling of an adventure from the Odyssey.
A man and woman sit in a sunny garden arbour, shaded by leaves. Gierymski painted the light dappling their faces. The work is relaxed and natural. It's a treasure of Polish art.

A man and woman sit on a bench in a glass-roofed garden room, surrounded by lush plants. Manet used the real-life couple, the Guillemets, who ran a shop. The woman wears a ring while the man leans toward her, with a gap between them. It's a subtle picture of two people.

A wide-eyed angel with wings seems to look back in surprise, drawn in a childlike style. Paul Klee made this in 1920, and philosopher Walter Benjamin later owned it and wrote about it as an angel of history. Benjamin saw the angel being blown backward into the future, looking at the pile of wreckage of the past. It's a famous image about time.

Horses, workers and a rising city explode in a blur of color and movement. Boccioni painted it as a celebration of the energetic new industrial city of Milan. He was a leader of Futurism, which loved speed and machines. It's one of the key paintings of the movement.

A maid carries a tray with a glass of water and a cup of hot chocolate, all painted with fine precision. Liotard worked in pastels and made this in Vienna. A Dresden collector bought it and it hangs in the Old Masters Gallery there. It's one of the most famous pastel paintings.

The Duke of Prussia kneels to swear loyalty to the king of Poland in Kraków's central square in 1525. Matejko packed it with portraits of nobles and knights in rich costumes. It's a picture of a time when Poland was strong. It's a national treasure.

Oedipus stands face to face with the Sphinx in a rocky pass, the monster clinging to his chest. Moreau's picture shows two figures locked in a deep stare. It was his first success at the Salon, in 1864. It's among the most famous Symbolist paintings.

Cupids and woodland figures dance in a flowery glade as spring returns. Bouguereau often painted fairy-tale scenes full of soft color and joyful movement. Nature wakes up after winter. It's a cheerful celebration of the season.

A young girl in a white dress sits in the shade of a tree, with a pretty village on a hill behind her. Bazille painted it at his family's home in Montpellier, in the south of France. The strong sunlight and shadows were new at the time. It's an early Impressionist masterpiece.

A widow kneels at the bed of her husband Hector, a hero of the Trojan War, with her young son by her side. David painted this scene from Homer's Iliad. It has a stark, heartbreaking feeling. It helped earn him membership at the French Academy.

paintings.m: Musée des Beaux-Arts de la ville de Paris
paintings.why: The Roman philosopher Seneca, ordered to take his own life by Emperor Nero, calmly dictates his last words to scribes as his friends weep. David painted a thoughtful, tragic scene early in his career. The story is about staying true to your values to the end. It's a powerful example of Neoclassical art.

A dark silhouette of a snake charmer plays a flute in a moonlit jungle, with glowing eyes and snakes coiled around. Rousseau said it was inspired by a friend's story of India. The painting is full of lush leaves painted in dozens of greens. It's a dreamlike masterpiece.

The goddess Venus rises from the sea, wearing a seashell like a hat, while cherubs frolic nearby. Gérôme was a great admirer of the classical world. He painted it late in his life. It's a lively picture of mythology.

Blossoming orchards line the foreground, with the old town of Arles and its stone towers behind them. Van Gogh was captivated by the spring in Provence. The painting glows with white and pink flowers. It's a happy picture of a fresh season.

Two women stand close together, one holding a bowl of flowers or fruit, in bright colors. Gauguin painted this in his later years in the Marquesas Islands. The flat, rich colors are a sign of his love of the Pacific. It's one of his best-known island paintings.

A crowd of workers marches steadily out of the shadows toward us. Pellizza spent years on this painting. He called it 'The Fourth Estate' because it showed the working class as a new force in society. It became a symbol of workers' rights in Italy.

paintings.m: Department of Paintings of the Louvre
paintings.why: The Spartan king Leonidas sits in calm readiness with his soldiers at the mountain pass of Thermopylae, preparing for a last stand against a vast Persian army. David painted the Spartans with heroic simplicity. In 480 BC, 300 Spartans and their allies held off the Persians for days. It's one of history's most famous last stands.

A man throws himself at the doorway, begging for Poland not to be divided, while the nobles in the room look away. Matejko painted a moment from 1773, when Poland's neighbors carved up the country. It's a harsh message about betrayal. It's a famous national symbol.

Sailboats with bright white sails glide across the Seine on a sunny day, with their reflections wobbling in the water. Monet lived at Argenteuil and painted boating there for years. The water ripples with strokes of color. It's one of his bright, breezy summer scenes.

A famous surgeon pauses in an operating theater to explain a procedure to a room of students, his hand bloody. Eakins's honest picture showed modern science. Many in 1875 found the realism hard to look at. Today it's seen as one of the greatest American paintings.

paintings.m: Department of Paintings of the Louvre
paintings.why: The Greek poet Homer sits at the center of a temple, crowned by a goddess of Victory, while the greatest writers, artists and thinkers from history gather around him. Ingres painted a tribute to the ancient world as a grand 'who's who.' The composition is very symmetrical and orderly. It was painted for a ceiling in the Louvre.

A group of painters, writers and friends raise their glasses in a sunny garden in Skagen, in northern Denmark. Krøyer painted his colony of artist friends, including himself. The light is warm and the mood is joyful. It's one of the best-loved Danish paintings.

paintings.m: Department of Paintings of the Louvre
paintings.why: Napoleon rides a mule on a mountain pass, looking rather calm, in a more realistic version of the heroic scene. Delaroche painted it in 1848 to show how it was in truth — a mule, not a prancing horse. It's a clever answer to David's famous idealized portrait. It reminds us that history can be told in different ways.

Giant figures float through the sky, with one holding scissors to cut the thread of life, like the Fates of Greek myth. It's one of Goya's Black Paintings on the walls of his home. The picture is also known as 'The Fates.' It's a spooky reflection on time and destiny.

A woman sits upright on a divan, painted with Modigliani's simplified, elegant, elongated shapes. He painted many such portraits in Paris in 1917. The curved lines and warm colors create a feeling of calm. It's an example of his unique style.
