A tangle of colored rectangles and lines tilts and floats on a white ground, like objects in space. Malevich created Suprematism to show pure feeling in shapes. The painting seems to drift in all directions. It's an exciting piece of early abstract art.

An open window frames a view of boats in a harbor, with window boxes of flowers and bursts of pure color. Matisse painted this in the summer of 1905 at Collioure on France's southern coast. It's a famous Fauvist painting. It invites us to look out at a bright new view.

A path leads through arches of irises, daylilies and roses in Monet's colorful garden. He designed the garden himself and painted it for decades. The mass of flowers is painted in joyful strokes. It's a glimpse of the paradise he built.

Dark birds perch in birch trees as a little church stands behind, and spring melts the snow. Savrasov painted this in a quiet village, and it became one of the most beloved Russian paintings. It's regarded as the start of a new feeling for Russian landscape. People love it for its quiet, simple beauty.

Three Russian knights on horseback, from folk tales, scan the horizon for danger. Vasnetsov painted Ilya Muromets, Dobrynya Nikitich and Alyosha Popovich, famous heroes. It took him nearly 20 years. Many Russian kids know this painting from school.

Young dancers stand and stretch in a practice studio, as the ballet master looks on. Degas loved to paint dancers behind the scenes, working hard. He painted many studies like this, with unusual views. It's one of his best-loved pictures.

A bush of lilacs stands in the garden of an asylum in Saint-Rémy, with a blue sky. Van Gogh painted this in the spring of 1889. The soft purples and blues contrast with the green leaves. It's a quiet picture of beauty in a hard time.

A man stands by a door, and a woman in a chemise sits sadly at the foot of a bed, in a dimly lit bedroom. Degas gave no title to explain the story, which makes people wonder. It's famous as a mysterious picture of tension between two people.

paintings.t: The Boy in the Red Vest
paintings.why: A young man in a red vest leans on his arm, painted in sculpted blocks of color. Cézanne painted this model, an Italian youth, several times. Look at his unnaturally long arm — it's deliberate, for the balance of the composition. It's one of the most famous modern portraits.

Two sisters in pink and blue dresses stand side by side, smiling softly. Renoir painted the daughters of a Parisian banker, Alice and Elisabeth Cahen d'Anvers. The soft colors and curls give them a sweet charm. It's a very sweet double portrait.

paintings.t: The Favourites of the Emperor Honorius
paintings.why: A Roman emperor feeds his pet chickens, which he called by the names of cities, while an official brings news. In the legend, he cared more for his hens than for the news that Rome was falling. Waterhouse painted a rich scene of the late Roman Empire. It's a funny and surprising story.

paintings.t: View of the Sea at Scheveningen
paintings.why: Dark waves roll under a gray sky, with a few small figures and boats on the beach. Van Gogh painted this on the Dutch coast in 1882, in the wind and sand. Tiny grains of sand are still stuck in the paint. It's an early, wild seascape.

A woman stretches her back after hours of needlework, in a room of rich blue and gold, with a stained-glass window. The painting is inspired by a poem by Tennyson about a woman waiting for a lover who doesn't come. Millais used glowing colors. It's a gorgeous Pre-Raphaelite painting.

A young woman reclines on a wave, with a pearl in her hand, as the surf and spray curl around her. Baudry painted it at the Paris Salon of 1863. The Empress Eugénie bought it. It's a charming picture of a water spirit.

paintings.t: The Hanging of the Sigismund bell at the Cathedral Tower in 1521 in Kraków
paintings.why: In 1521 in Kraków, workers raise a giant bell by ropes into the cathedral tower, as the crowd and the king watch. The Sigismund Bell is still in the cathedral and still rings. Matejko painted the pride of the city. It's a lively picture of a big community project.

Dozens of gentlemen crowd into a famous gallery in Florence, studying paintings and statues from the Renaissance. Queen Charlotte commissioned Zoffany to paint the picture, and he squeezed in masterpieces from all over the museum. He arranged the artworks and people as he liked. It's a picture of a museum filled with art.

A long avenue of poplars glows with yellow and orange autumn light, with strolling couples. It was an ancient Roman cemetery in Arles, France. Van Gogh painted it in autumn 1888. The golden trees seem to dance.

A fashionable woman in a pink, patterned dress looks out in front of a bright, richly colored background. Klimt painted her a second time, years after his gold portrait. This one is colorful instead of golden. It sold for $88 million in 2006.

A woman holds a flower and an apple, with a golden background, her mouth beckoning. The title means 'the kissed mouth.' Rossetti used her red hair and rich fabrics in a daring new style. It started a new direction in his painting.

A stylish young woman in a deep blue dress and a flowered hat looks out with a confident smile. Renoir painted it in 1874 in the first year of Impressionism. The blue fabric glimmers in the light. It's an elegant picture of the modern city.

A woman stands in the shadows with a large snake draped over her shoulders, her eyes glowing. Franz von Stuck painted this as a symbol of temptation. It was a huge success, and he painted several versions. It is a dark and dramatic Symbolist painting.

A woman in a bright red Japanese kimono stands with a fan against a background of fans. Monet's wife Camille posed for it. Japanese art was a craze in Paris in the 1870s. It's a colorful, playful piece.

According to legend, Lady Godiva rode a horse through the town in protest of a harsh tax, and the townspeople kindly stayed indoors. Collier painted her in a hush of dignity. The tale is a famous English legend. It's a picture of courage.

paintings.t: The Lady with a Fan, The Artist's Wife
paintings.why: A woman in a splendid blue satin gown holds a fan, with a calm smile. Roslin painted his wife Marie-Suzanne Giroust, a talented artist herself. The shimmering fabric is a marvel. It's one of the great portraits of the 1700s.

A crab lies on its back, its claws and legs curled, in a few strokes of orange and green. Van Gogh was inspired by Japanese prints and painted it in Paris. It's a quick but lively study. It shows he could find wonder in simple things.

A large woman steps out of a pond as her companion watches, in a Realist take on a classical theme. When it was shown in 1853, critics and the emperor were scandalized. Courbet liked to shock. It's a famous painting about honesty and realism.

A couple's faces merge into one in a dim room, beside a window with a glimmer of light. Munch painted several versions of the scene. The way the two become one is touching and mysterious. It's one of his best-loved paintings.

Van Gogh looks out with a bandage over his ear, wearing a fur cap and a thick coat, with a Japanese print behind him. He painted it after he hurt his ear in December 1888. It's a direct, honest picture of a difficult time. It's among the most famous self-portraits.

A hundred horses graze, rest, swim and gallop across a long scroll, a mix of Chinese and Italian styles. Castiglione, an Italian monk painter at the Chinese court, painted it for the emperor. It shows how different art traditions can combine. It's one of the treasures of Chinese court art.

paintings.m: Musée des Beaux-Arts de la ville de Paris
paintings.why: A young Courbet sits in the countryside with his dog, leaning against a rock, looking out with confidence. He painted this when he was 23. The dark landscape gives the picture a moody feeling. It's an early display of his talent.

Two nuns in a convent graveyard at twilight, one digging a grave, the other sitting nearby. Millais painted it near London, with a sunset sky. The still, silent mood is unforgettable. It's a haunting view of quiet devotion.

paintings.m: Department of Paintings of the Louvre
paintings.why: A young girl in a white dress and a soft yellow shawl looks gently out of the canvas. Ingres painted her when she was about 13, and the smooth, curving lines and delicate details show his skill. She died only a year later, which adds a sad note to the portrait. It's one of the most loved portraits of a child.

A man draws back in surprise as a captive starling, which can only say 'I can't get out,' flutters in a cage. The painting was inspired by a story by Laurence Sterne. Wright of Derby used lamplight to bring the moment to life. It makes you think about freedom and kindness.

A soldier in a black uniform says a tender, hasty goodbye to his sweetheart before riding off to battle, just before Waterloo. She holds the door shut as if she could keep him back. Millais painted every fold of her satin dress. It was one of the most popular paintings of its day.

paintings.m: Department of Paintings of the Louvre
paintings.why: Four racehorses are stretched out in mid-gallop, all their legs off the ground, with jockeys in bright colors. Géricault painted the 'flying gallop' at a time before cameras could show how horses really run. We now know that this is not how horses really move! It's a thrilling picture of speed that influenced later artists.

Two girls in black dresses stand with rosy cheeks and shining hair. Renoir painted them with warm light, with a touch of the outdoors in the colors. They are two of his favorite young models. It's a charming picture of youth.

paintings.t: Madame Georges Charpentier and her Children
paintings.why: A wealthy publisher's wife sits with her young son and daughter, and a large dog on a couch, in a room with Japanese decor. Renoir's painting won him new patrons when it was well received at the Salon. It's fabulously cozy. It's a portrait of a stylish Paris family.

paintings.t: Portrait of Antoine-Laurent Lavoisier and his wife
paintings.why: A famous chemist sits at a table of scientific instruments, as his wife leans on his shoulder. Lavoisier helped create modern chemistry, and his wife Marie-Anne was his partner in science. David painted them as a pair of modern, smart people. It's a landmark portrait of science.

Dark, flame-shaped cypress trees twist up toward a swirling sky. Van Gogh said they were as beautiful as an Egyptian obelisk. He painted several versions during his stay in Saint-Rémy. They've become signature elements of his art.

A Highland soldier, freed from prison, gives the jailer the order to release him, while his wife, with a baby in her arms, rests her head on his shoulder. Millais used his future wife as the model. The picture earned him the greatest success of his career. It's an emotional tale of reunion.

The boy Icarus, who flew too close to the sun, lies on the shore as sea nymphs mourn. In the Greek myth, his wax wings melted. Draper painted the beautiful, glowing scene in 1898. It's one of the most beloved paintings of Greek myth.

paintings.m: Department of Paintings of the Louvre
paintings.why: A man locks a door with one arm, as a woman tries to push him away and to reach a table with an apple in the background. Fragonard painted it in 1777. The sparkle of the fabrics is dazzling. The meaning is mysterious, so viewers still debate it.

A man in a black coat and hat stands with a paintbrush and palette in front of a harbor and a ship decorated with flags. Rousseau painted himself as a proud artist in the world. The hot-air balloon and flags show his sense of fun. It's a charming self-portrait.

paintings.t: Entry of the Crusaders in Constantinople
paintings.m: Department of Paintings of the Louvre
paintings.why: Crusader knights ride through a city in 1204, with crowds of people begging for mercy. Delacroix painted the wildness of history in swirling colors. The painting hangs in the Louvre. It's a tough scene, painted with deep emotion.

A whirlwind of colors, shapes and lines swirls across the whole canvas. Kandinsky made dozens of studies for it and painted it in just four days. He believed that color and shape could move us like music. It's often called his masterpiece and one of the first great abstract paintings.

paintings.t: Cleopatra Testing Poisons on Condemned Prisoners
paintings.why: The Egyptian queen watches closely as a poison is tested on prisoners, while her servants stand by. Cabanel painted a gripping scene of the ancient world. The details of the room are exquisite. It's a dramatic image of ancient power.
l: Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp

paintings.why: The god Jupiter sits on his throne, with an eagle by his side, while the sea-goddess Thetis begs a favor. Ingres painted it at age 31 in Rome. The great size and the strict calm made some critics unhappy. It's a bold act of artistic ambition.

A young Jesus, working in a carpenter's shop, stretches out his arms, and the shadow forms a cross on the wall behind. His mother looks on, feeling fear. Hunt painted it in the Holy Land. It's one of the most famous images of Jesus as a boy.

A British general dies on the battlefield after winning the Battle of Quebec in 1759, as officers gather around him like figures in a religious painting. Benjamin West dressed the scene in contemporary clothes, which was bold at the time. The painting was a sensation in London. It changed how history painting was done.
A smiling young woman in a colorful dress and headscarf leans her head on her hand. Bouguereau painted her with great care. It's a pleasant, charming portrait. It shows how popular his work was.

A lone goat stands on the salt shore of the Dead Sea, with a red cloth on its horns. In an old tradition, a goat carried the sins of the people into the wilderness. Hunt traveled to the Dead Sea to paint it on the spot. It's famous for its harsh, shimmering landscape.

At dawn in the snow, a man in a white Pierrot costume is held by his friend after losing a duel. The story's details are uncertain, but the picture was a hit with the public. The harsh cold and the colorful costumes make it unforgettable. It's a fine example of dramatic storytelling.

A huge old oak stands in a meadow under a gloomy sky, with a pale village and hills beyond. Friedrich painted the tree like a hero, strong but alone. It's a symbol of survival. It's one of his best-known landscapes.

Two men sit by a chessboard in a quiet room, thinking deeply. Eakins painted his father and friends and was mindful of the light on the wood and on their faces. It was a gift to his father. It's a nice study of concentration.

A young girl in a ragged dress stands in a field of tall grass, with a pair of large eyes and a sad, direct look. Bouguereau made many pictures of poor children for rich collectors. It's meant to inspire compassion. It's still a famous image of childhood.

A young man in a hat stands by a table, in a studio with a suit of armor and a mother-and-child nearby. Manet's son Léon posed. The scene doesn't tell a clear story, which keeps people curious. It's a modern, mysterious indoor scene.

A basket of apples sits tilted on a table with a bottle, a plate of biscuits and a cloth, painted from several angles at once. Cézanne wanted to show how we actually see, with our eyes moving around. The table looks tilted and the bottle too. It's a great example of his groundbreaking approach.

A skeleton gardener in a black cloak waters flowers as a boy and girl in white watch. Simberg's strange, gentle painting turns death into a friendly gardener. He was a Finnish Symbolist painter. It's both spooky and sweet.

A young woman in a blue gown and a young man kneel together with a trailing rose bush, a shy and sad moment. Hughes painted it in a very fine detail with rich color. The painting is based on a poem by Tennyson. It's a dreamy scene of first love.

A white farmhouse sits among golden fields and green trees under a bright blue sky. Van Gogh painted it in Arles in summer 1888. The bold color and clean lines show his Japanese influences. It's a sunny scene of country life.

Two men sink up to their knees in mud, striking each other with sticks, as a dark landscape stretches behind them. Goya painted this on the wall of his house in his Black Paintings series. It's often seen as a picture of conflict that goes nowhere. It's a serious, thoughtful painting.

Great wooden ships fire their guns in a smoky sea battle, as sailors battle on deck and in the water. Turner painted this scene from the Royal Navy's 1805 victory, in which Admiral Nelson died. It was commissioned for King George IV. It's a record of a famous naval battle.

A view over Paris rooftops in the snow, with chimneys and gray skies. Caillebotte painted it from the window of his home. The cool colors and unusual view are quiet and modern. It's a favorite of city landscapes.

A girl in a white dress stands in a field of wheat in the sun, with her back slightly turned. Van Gogh painted it in Auvers-sur-Oise in 1890. The brushwork is lively and bright. It's a peaceful piece from his final weeks.

The holy city shines golden in the late sun, seen from the Mount of Olives. Gérôme visited the Middle East and painted the scene with great fidelity. Its calm and glowing mood makes the city feel timeless. It's a majestic view.

paintings.t: Empress Eugenie Surrounded by her Ladies in Waiting
paintings.why: The Empress of France sits on a flower-strewn lawn, with her ladies in pastel gowns gathered around, like in a garden party. Winterhalter was the favorite portrait painter of royalty across Europe. The picture has a dreamy, fairy-tale glow. It's a glimpse into royal life.

A woman at a dressing table powders her face in front of a vase of flowers. Seurat painted his partner Madeleine Knobloch, and he later painted over a portrait of himself in the corner. It's made with fine dots, with a flat, decorative look. It's a quiet, witty picture.

The queen of France sits proudly with her children, and an empty cradle. Vigée Le Brun painted it to improve the queen's image, at a time when people were angry with her. The empty cradle represents a baby daughter who had recently died. It's a sad and important portrait.

Five red figures stand on a green hill under a deep blue sky, singing and playing. Matisse used just three colors: blue, green and red. The simplicity and boldness were revolutionary. It's a masterpiece of modern color.

A woman reclines on a bed in a Tahitian room, as a raven sits by the window and two people whisper in the background. Gauguin named it after a poem by Edgar Allan Poe. The mood is mysterious and moody. It's a rich picture of colors and symbols.

Young people in fancy clothes play the game of blind man's bluff in a ring, outdoors. Goya painted it as a design for a tapestry for the Spanish palace. The light and fun scene is full of charm. It's a happy picture from his early career.

Dancers kick up their legs in a lively Paris cabaret dance, with a musician and the audience. Seurat painted it with tiny dots of color, and the lines all lead upward for cheerfulness. The effect is a moving, energetic scene. It's one of the best examples of his method.

paintings.t: Miss La La at the Cirque Fernando
paintings.why: A circus performer hangs by her teeth from a rope high in the air, as the audience looks up from below. Degas made it after seeing her perform in Paris. The dizzying angle and the geometry of the dome are daring. It's an exciting picture.

A group of boys march and play with toy drums and swords. Goya painted this as a design for a tapestry, with bright colors and lively movement. It's a charming glimpse of children at play in 1700s Spain. It captures the joy of imagination.

A young doctor sits in a swirling background of red, orange and green. Dr. Rey treated Van Gogh in the hospital in Arles. Van Gogh gave him the portrait, but the doctor wasn't a fan and used it to patch a chicken coop, the story goes. Today it's worth a fortune.

People in bright clothes crowd the stands of a Roman arena for a bullfight, under a blue sky. Van Gogh was struck by the old structure and the festive crowd. The painting is made of bold dabs of color. It's a lively scene of Provençal life.

paintings.m: Department of Paintings of the Louvre
paintings.why: The prince Paris sits beside Helen of Troy, with Cupid close by, in a graceful chamber. According to legend, their love began the Trojan War. David painted it in 1788 in the elegant style of ancient Greece. It's a beautiful scene with a sad ending to come.

A boy kneels to drink from a pond, as sheep and a dog wait on a path, bordered by a golden cornfield. Constable painted the place he knew from his childhood. The rich greens and the glowing sky are full of life. It's a classic of English landscape.

A woman with dignity and calm looks out at us, wearing a white head covering and a draped shawl. Bilińska, a Polish painter who trained in Paris, painted this in 1884. It was a portrait that treated its sitter with respect, at a time when that was uncommon. It's a striking example of 19th-century portrait painting.

A young woman, Mary, sits on a bed in a plain white room as the angel Gabriel appears. Rossetti used only white and blue, a bold choice. The title means 'Behold the handmaid of the Lord.' It was a fresh, modern view of a very old story.

Rooftops, chimneys and a cloudy sky stretch over Paris as seen from the apartment where Van Gogh lived with his brother Theo. Van Gogh painted the view in 1887 with fresh, quick strokes after learning from the Impressionists. It's one of the first signs of his bright palette. It's a city view with a feeling of home.

A woman in a long white dress holds a flower to her ear, in warm tropical light. Gauguin painted it soon after arriving in Tahiti. The simple, strong figure and bold colors show his new direction. It's a famous image of his first stay on the island.

Two figures, one wading and one on the beach, are near the sea in Tahiti, with a pink tree arching overhead. The title means 'near the sea.' Gauguin built the picture out of flat, bold areas of color, like a Japanese print. It's a dreamy view of paradise.

A merchant, Sadko, is walking along the sea bottom in a magical underwater kingdom, as the Sea King's daughters parade past in dresses. It's based on a Russian folk tale, which inspired an opera, too. Repin painted the sea princesses with different faces from many nations. It's a fairy tale full of beauty.

A priest preaches to the king and nobles of Poland about their duties, warning them of dangers ahead. Piotr Skarga was a real preacher in the 1500s who warned of a decline. Matejko painted it to inspire Poles in a time of foreign rule. It's famous for its message of patriotism.

Dancing figures in a circle, in a lively swirl of ancient costume. Bouguereau's graceful figures seem to move to music. It's a classical celebration of dance as part of life. The smooth surface and gentle poses are signatures of his style.

A woman sits in front of a mirror, brushing her long golden hair, in a rich red-and-white room. In old legend, Lilith was Adam's first wife. Rossetti's painting is full of beautiful details, like flowers and a glowing mirror. It's a dreamy picture of beauty and mystery.

Moss-covered roofs of old cottages cluster together in a village, with trees and a cloudy sky. Van Gogh painted it in Auvers-sur-Oise, in northern France, in 1890. He loved these old thatched houses. It reminds you of simple country life.

A sunny path curves through green fields lined with trees near the town of Arles. Van Gogh painted the bright scene in the summer light of southern France. The path draws the viewer into the picture. It's a peaceful stroll.

Artists and friends gather in a bright studio full of paintings, including Manet, Monet and Renoir. Bazille painted the group that would form the Impressionists. The painting shows his friends before they became famous. It's like a family snapshot of art history.

A little girl sits in a landscape, her head tilted, with a sweet look of curiosity. Reynolds was the first president of the Royal Academy, and he often painted children. The soft light and fluffy dress capture childhood. It's one of the best-loved child portraits in English art.

paintings.t: The Ambassadors of Agamemnon in the tent of Achilles
paintings.why: Greek messengers come to the tent of the hero Achilles, who sulks over a quarrel with his commander, begging him to return to the war. Ingres painted it at 20, as a prize piece in Paris. It's based on Homer's Iliad. It shows how well he'd learned the lessons of ancient sculpture.

A pale man stares out in the foreground of a garden as a couple stands behind him. Munch painted jealousy as a green-faced mood. The painting is more about feeling than action. It's a revealing look at a strong emotion.

A knight leans down from his horse as his lady ties a scarf around his arm and wishes him luck before battle. Edmund Blair Leighton painted such romantic scenes from the Middle Ages with great detail. This one is among the most popular. It's a picture of love and courage.

A crowd of people with ghostly faces walk toward us under a blood-red sky on a bridge. Munch made this just after his most famous painting, The Scream, with similar colors. The mood is one of unease. It's a picture of worry that many people recognize.

Two polar bears prowl through the wreck of an Arctic expedition, gnawing at a torn flag and scattered supplies. Landseer painted this after the lost Franklin expedition. The title means we make plans but nature has the final say. It's a famous and very dramatic image.

paintings.t: Joséphine-Éléonore-Marie-Pauline de Galard de Brassac de Béarn (1825–1860), Princesse de Broglie
paintings.why: A French princess sits in a blue satin dress with a pearl necklace and elegant poise. Ingres took a long time to paint her, and the dress is exquisitely detailed. The portrait is one of the most admired of the 1800s. It hangs in the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York.

Sheep graze on a bright green cliff above a blue sea, with sunlight on their wool. Hunt painted every blade of grass and animal in close detail. It was meant as a warning of an invasion — the sheep, he joked, were unprotected. It's a beautiful look at the English coast.

After being stabbed by senators in Rome, Julius Caesar's body lies in a theater, while the conspirators scatter. Gérôme painted an empty hall instead of the actual fight. The still, quiet scene is more haunting than a battle. It's a clever painting of a famous event.

Two crabs, one on its back, scuttle on a pale green background. Van Gogh painted them in Arles in 1889, using bright orange and green. He loved Japanese prints, which have many pictures of sea life. It's a charming study.
A young girl with red hair looks out with soft, grave eyes, wearing a white dress. Bouguereau painted her in 1890. The soft realism is typical of his work. It's a sensitive portrait of a child.

A man in a green coat holds a violin as he glances out, with a bow in his hand. Anne Vallayer-Coster was a French painter, and one of the few women admitted to the French Royal Academy of Painting. She was famous for still lifes, and this is an unusual portrait. It's a lovely picture of music.

A crowd of 42 cats, each with a different personality, poses on and around a luxurious cushion. Carl Kahler painted the cats of a rich woman in San Francisco, and the painting took three years. The cats' names are known, and the painting is a world record in cat portraits. It's a delight for cat lovers.

A woman looks over her shoulder with a bold stare, wearing a patterned robe, set against a pale background. Klimt painted it at the end of his career. It was stolen from a museum in Italy in 1997 and mysteriously reappeared in 2019. It's one of the strangest art stories.

A woman with a snake wound around her body stands by a tree in a lush forest. John Collier painted Lilith, a character from old legends. The snake and soft light give it a dreamlike feel. It's an eye-catching Victorian painting.

A young woman in a white dress stands before a background of Chinese-style patterns and figures. Klimt painted Elisabeth when she was around 17. The decorations are inspired by East Asian art. It's a stunning portrait filled with ornament.

paintings.t: Mademoiselle V. . . in the Costume of an Espada
paintings.why: A woman dressed as a bullfighter holds a pink cape in a studio, with a little fight scene behind her. Manet's model, Victorine Meurent, is the same woman from 'Olympia'. It's a playful picture of costume and performance. It shows his love of Spanish art.

A bird rises above a golden field of waving wheat under a wide sky. Van Gogh painted it in Paris in 1887, and the field swirls in lively brushstrokes. He loved the open countryside. It's a happy, breezy landscape.

The cathedral's slim spire rises beyond a stream and meadow beneath a stormy sky, with a bright rainbow. Constable painted it in 1831, when he was sad about the death of his wife. The dramatic clouds show his feelings. It's one of his grandest landscapes.

Bazille's family are posed on a terrace under the trees at their home in southern France. He painted them in strong sunlight, looking out in rows. The picture was accepted at the Salon of 1868. It's an early step in Impressionism.

paintings.t: Landscape with a Carriage and a Train
paintings.why: A horse-drawn carriage races across a golden field, as a train steams by in the distance, under a cloudy sky. Van Gogh painted it in 1890 in his last weeks. The old and new world are side by side. It's a lively, energetic view of the countryside.
The elderly Goya, ill and pale, is held by his doctor, who offers him a drink. Goya painted it as thanks to Dr. Arrieta for saving his life. Dark shadows loom behind them. It's a touching tribute.

An old, blind general, once a great hero, begs on the street as a soldier recognizes him in astonishment. In the story, Belisarius was Rome's top commander who was treated unfairly. David painted it with clear and strong emotions. It's a lesson that glory can vanish.

paintings.t: The Death of Leonardo da Vinci
paintings.m: Musée des Beaux-Arts de la ville de Paris
paintings.why: The great artist Leonardo da Vinci lies on his deathbed in France, in the arms of the king, as friends look on. It's a legend, not a proven fact, but Ingres loved the story. The painting is a tribute to a genius. It reflects the great respect for artists in 1800s France.

The hero Achilles is furious as Agamemnon takes back a prize, in a scene from Homer's Iliad. David painted it late in his life, in exile, in a rich, sculpted style. The rage is felt in every face. It's a dramatic moment from the Trojan War.
Women in the Tahitian countryside play music under a red dog's gaze, with a spirit figure in the background. 'Arearea' means 'joyousness.' Gauguin's colors are bold and flat. It's a dreamy scene.

A barefoot young girl in a rural dress stands in a green field, with a gentle, direct look. Bouguereau painted idealized peasant girls that were very popular. This one is shown with soft, smooth finish. It's a typical beloved image.

A dark, ghostly crowd of people sing, stagger and stare out in a wild procession. Goya painted it on a wall of his house as part of the Black Paintings. It's a contrast with his earlier cheerful version of the same festival. It shows how his view of the world had darkened.

Figures relax on a beach in dots of purple, orange and blue, around a table with a picnic, beneath the bright sun. Matisse got the title from a poem by Baudelaire. He used the dots of Seurat but made them bigger and wilder. It was an important step toward Fauvism.

A magnificent chestnut horse rears up against a plain background, the size of life. Stubbs painted it for the Marquess of Rockingham, and it is thought that there was no background by design. His knowledge of horse anatomy is astonishing. It is the most famous horse painting in Britain.

A queen in black stands by the coffin of her husband, refusing to let it be buried, in a bleak landscape. Joanna of Castile was the Queen of Spain and was said to be overwhelmed with grief. Pradilla painted the scene in a vast, wild setting. It's a famous work from Spain.

paintings.m: Royal Academy of Fine Arts of San Fernando
paintings.why: A crowd in masks and costumes dance and shout in a wild carnival procession. Goya painted it in the 1810s, a festival at the end of Carnival in Madrid. The faces are strange and frightening. It's an energetic piece.
l: Royal Academy of Fine Arts of San Fernando

paintings.t: Portrait of the Marchioness of Santa Cruz
paintings.why: A Spanish noblewoman lies on a couch, in a classical white dress, with a lyre, as if she were a Muse. Goya painted it with loose brushstrokes and with a cool and gentle mood. It's an original and fresh view of portraits. It's a favorite in Madrid's Prado Museum.

In the dark cellar of a Roman arena, slaves drag the bodies of fallen gladiators away, as crowds look on. Juan Luna from the Philippines won the top prize at an art show in Madrid in 1884 with this huge painting, among the biggest in the world. Filipinos were proud that one of their own beat the best European artists. It's a national treasure of the Philippines.

paintings.t: Little Girl in a Blue Armchair
paintings.why: A girl slouches in a big blue armchair in a living room, looking bored, with a sleeping dog in another chair. Cassatt painted a child's real attitude instead of making her look perfect. Degas helped with the painting, they say. It's one of the most famous paintings of childhood.

A church on a small island in Venice glows pink and gold, and the water shimmers in purple and blue. Monet painted it in 1908 on a trip with his wife, and he finished some of the pictures at home. The colors melt like a dream. It's a lovely view of an unforgettable city.

Four bright blue horses stand huddled together in a landscape of red, yellow and purple. Franz Marc believed animals were pure and innocent, and he used colors to show feelings, not to match real life. The painting disappeared during World War II and has never been found. It is one of the most famous lost paintings.

Thatched farmhouses sit beside a golden wheat field and a path, under a bright blue sky with a swirl of clouds. Van Gogh painted it near Paris in the last weeks of his life. The roofs are in warm greens and reds. It's a happy look at rural life.

A couple stands arm in arm and smiles, the man holding his wife's arm. Renoir painted his friend, the Impressionist Alfred Sisley, and his future wife, Eugénie. It's a tender portrait of friendship and love. It's a fond record of an artist and his companion.

A woman in a white dress sits by a window, reading, as a man looks away from a book at her. Manet's wife, Suzanne, posed for it. The painting is calm and gentle. It's a pleasant moment of a quiet day.

A curving river winds through a green valley as a storm clears. A tiny painter at an easel stands on the hillside in the corner. Thomas Cole showed that nature was big and beautiful, and humans were small. It's one of the most famous American landscape paintings.

A girl in a dark dress stands among tall beech trees with brown leaves. Van Gogh painted it in the Netherlands when he was starting out. The mix of light and shadow is lively. It's a rustic look at an early painting.

paintings.t: Jeune Fille au piano (Girl at the Piano - The Overture to Tannhauser)
paintings.why: A young woman sits at a piano, playing, as an older woman sews in a rocking chair. Cézanne painted his sister and mother in a bold, flat way. The famous music of Wagner's Tannhäuser was the inspiration. It's a quiet moment in a family.

A young noblewoman in a pale dress with a feathery hairdo sits with her hands folded, wearing a soft, thoughtful look. Goya painted her when she was about 20, a few years after she'd been forced into a marriage. He saw the sadness in her eyes, and the portrait is full of feeling. It's one of his greatest portraits.

A boy in a white shirt and a big hat carries a sword that's too big for him, with a bright sash and pale background. Manet painted it as a young artist, inspired by the Spanish masters. It's both charming and bold. It's an early favorite.

The hero Ulysses is lashed to the mast of his ship as bird-women, the sirens, swoop and sing to lure him. His crew, ears plugged, row on. Waterhouse painted the sirens with a wild energy. It's a famous scene from the Odyssey.

An old philosopher in a red hat sits reading by the light of a single lamp, which makes his face glow in the dark. Wright of Derby was a master of dramatic candlelight. The picture makes you think about the quiet joy of studying. It's a model of strong light and shadow.

Mary floats in a pale blue gown, standing on a crescent moon and surrounded by angels, in a cloud of golden light. Tiepolo painted it for a church in Madrid. The airy colors make the whole scene look like it's floating. It's one of the most graceful paintings of the Baroque era.

A woman in a blue dress, her hands in her lap, sits with a steady look. Cézanne painted her in a patchwork of blue and tan strokes. His later portraits are made of blocks of color. It's an example of his simple but powerful way of painting.

Two girls in a forest rest after gathering nuts, one of them sitting with a basket and the other reclining. Bouguereau was a master of smooth, careful finish. The fresh-faced girls seem to glow in the green woods. It's a sweet, natural scene.

paintings.t: King Cophetua and the Beggar Maid
paintings.why: A king sits on the steps of his throne, wearing golden armor, gazing up at a barefoot beggar girl who holds a flower. According to a legend, he fell in love with her and made her his queen. Burne-Jones painted a glittering, richly decorated scene. It's a fairy tale in paint.

A tall iron bridge crosses a train station, with a man in a top hat looking over the rail. Caillebotte painted the new Paris of steel and steam. The perspective lines pull you into the picture. It's one of the first paintings about industry and the city.

paintings.t: General Johnson Saving a Wounded French Officer from the Tomahawk of a North American Indian
paintings.why: In a scene from the French and Indian War, a British officer protects a wounded French soldier. Benjamin West, an American in London, painted it with dramatic action in the forest. It shows kindness in a time of war. It's an early work of American-born art.

The hero Jason watches as the sorceress Medea mixes a magic potion to help him win the Golden Fleece. Waterhouse painted her in a rich turquoise gown, with a cauldron and flames. The picture is filled with mystery. It's a favorite of fans of Greek legends.

A shepherd flirts with a girl in a sunlit field as the sheep stray into the wheat. Hunt painted each leaf, each tuft of wool, in vivid color. He meant it as a lesson about neglecting duty. It's a joyous, detailed picture.

A pitcher, a fruit bowl and a patterned curtain are arranged on a table, with apples and peaches that seem to tilt. Cézanne changed the viewpoint on purpose, as if he moved while painting. It's like a puzzle made of color. It helped lead the way to Cubism.

A boy gazes at a soap bubble he has just blown, with a dreamy look. Millais painted it as a picture of his grandson, 'A Child's World.' It was later used in a soap advertisement, which made it one of the most famous paintings ever. It's a well-known image of childhood wonder.

Pink roses burst from a vase against a pale green background. Van Gogh painted it in Auvers-sur-Oise in his final months. The roses were originally a bright pink, though the color has faded. It's a lovely flower painting.

Winged spirits carry the maiden Psyche up into the sky in a swirl of silks. In the story, she's taken to a palace where she meets Cupid. Bouguereau painted a beautiful, soft scene. It's an enchanting picture of ancient myth.

A farming couple takes a nap in the shade of a haystack, with their tools beside them. Van Gogh copied the design of a Millet print and put it into his own bold colors. He said it was like translating into another language. It shows his love for the painter Millet.

A young woman sits on a grassy bank with a little dog on her lap, as a young man holds a bright green parasol over her. Goya designed this as a pattern for a tapestry for a royal palace. The colors are cheerful and bright. It's a delightful picture of leisure.
l: Museo Nacional Centro de Arte Reina Sofía

paintings.t: A Girl with a Watering Can
paintings.why: A little girl in a blue dress holds a watering can on a path with flowers and dappled light. Renoir captured a child's quiet game in a garden. It's very peaceful and sweet. The painting is in the National Gallery of Art in Washington.

A calm sunset glows red and gold behind a quiet landscape, with black trees on the horizon. Friedrich painted this late in life. The quiet colors remind us of the end of a day. It's a gentle painting.

A single big black circle sits on a white square. Malevich painted it as a partner to his Black Square, and it might be a symbol of a wheel or of a whole world. It was among the boldest artworks of the 1920s. It's a minimal abstraction.

A bird-woman with a swan's wings looks back over her shoulder against a darkening sky, wearing a jeweled crown. Vrubel painted the Swan Princess from a Russian opera, and his wife sang the role. The shimmering colors look like mosaic. It's one of the most captivating Russian fairy-tale paintings.

A big black ox pulls a farm cart across a field, under a stormy sky. Van Gogh painted the dark, heavy earth colors in the Netherlands when he lived with his parents. The ox seems strong and patient. It's an early look at rural labor.

A young woman in a flowing robe struggles against the cold north wind, represented by Boreas. In Greek myth, Boreas was the god of the north wind. Waterhouse painted him coming from the cloud with a mighty gust. It's a magical picture of weather.

A wild-eyed man rides a rearing black horse that tramples a woman, in a vivid painting of passion. Podkowiński made this in 1894 and showed it in Warsaw, where it caused a huge uproar. He eventually slashed it with a knife. It's a famous Polish Symbolist painting.

A shy girl wearing a blue-and-white headscarf looks out with a sweet, solemn face. The girl, Angelina, was a street kid in Venice who sold flowers. The painting won a top prize at an exhibition in 1897. It became one of the most-copied pictures in Italy.

A group of figures, with pointed hats, fly through the sky as they hold up a man, in a swirl of eerie blue and gray. Goya painted a world of superstition and fear. It's meant to make people think about the foolish things people believe. It's a spooky picture.

A man in a straw hat and a woman in a blue dress sit in a sailboat on a sparkling river, painted in a very bold crop. Manet painted it in the summer of 1874 at Argenteuil with Monet nearby. The blue water fills most of the canvas. It's a refreshing scene.

paintings.t: Woman with a Pearl Necklace in a Loge
paintings.why: A woman in a pale dress with a pearl necklace sits in a theater box, leaning forward and holding a fan. Cassatt painted this for the 1879 Impressionist show, with the glow of the theater lamps. She looks across at the audience while being observed herself. It's a picture of a woman who is clever and independent.

A French countess leans on her hand with a thoughtful look, in a satin blue dress. Ingres painted her over three years, and the textures of the flowers and silk are exquisite. A mirror shows the back of her head. It's a famous painting in the Frick Collection in New York.

A straw hat lies on a wall in dark shadows, painted with little dashes. Van Gogh worked on it in the Netherlands. The hat is a cheerful sign of summer. It's a small, humble object painted with affection.

Two winged brothers from Greek myth, Sleep and Death, lie side by side on a bed of poppies, in a quiet, dreamy pose. Waterhouse painted them in a haze of purple and gold. Sleep is the one who clutches a poppy. It's a peaceful picture of a serious subject.

A group of men sit relaxed around a table in a warm room after dinner, one of them playing a violin. Courbet painted his friends and his father in a dark, calm space. The painting won him a medal and was bought by the state. It's the start of his fame.

paintings.t: Ceremonial Sitting of the State Council on 7 May 1901 Marking the Centenary of its Foundation
paintings.why: Dozens of officials in uniform sit and stand in a vast hall, in a massive group portrait for the 100th anniversary of Russia's State Council. Repin painted 81 individual portraits with the help of his students. It's a record-setting giant canvas, over 4 meters tall. It's a window into a world that was about to vanish.

A woman in a theatrical pose leans on a stone, holding a cup, in a wild forest. In ancient times, a bacchante was a follower of the wine god. Courbet painted it early in his career, in a Romantic manner. It's an experiment before he turned to Realism.

A young woman in a white dress sits by the shore, looking out, with her hair in the breeze. Munch painted his sister Inger at the seaside in Norway. The peaceful mood is a contrast with his later, anxious paintings. It's a tender early portrait.

Van Gogh stands in a heavy coat and hat, with a bandage on his ear, and a pipe, looking calm. The painting shows him in a moment of recovery after a hard time. A bold orange background and strong lines make it memorable. It's a direct, honest self-portrait.

paintings.t: The Destruction of Sodom And Gomorrah
paintings.why: Fire rains from a stormy sky over a city of towers while tiny figures flee across a bridge. John Martin painted spectacular disasters from the Bible that thrilled huge crowds in Victorian England. His giant scenes were like the movies of their day. It's a famous piece of apocalyptic art.

The Egyptian queen sails in a golden barge, dressed as the goddess Venus, to meet Mark Antony in Tarsus. Etty painted the shimmering scene with rich color and flowing movement. The sails, flowers and attendants are dazzling. It's a lush picture of ancient glamour.

Two boys sit together in a room, drawing at a table, absorbed in their work. Sofie Ribbing, a Swedish painter, painted a quiet scene of children learning. The soft lighting and calm mood make it feel real. It's a gentle moment of creativity.

At dawn, a firing squad has just shot a French marshal, who lies on the ground by a wall, while the soldiers walk away. Gérôme left out the actual moment, showing only the aftermath. It's a quiet, strong picture about the end of an era. It's a haunting painting of history.

paintings.t: The Battle of the Kearsarge and the Alabama
paintings.why: Two warships fire at each other in the English Channel off Cherbourg in 1864, during the American Civil War. Manet, a Paris artist, painted a big wide sea with a tiny ship, and the Alabama sinking. The sea is a green-gray ocean with a high horizon. It's his first major seascape.

paintings.m: Department of Paintings of the Louvre
paintings.why: A gnarled, leafless oak stands in a field with a flock of black crows above it, under a pale sky. Friedrich painted bare trees that stood for strength and loneliness. The twisting branches are drawn with great care. It's a dramatic look at the bleakness of winter.

paintings.t: Peasant Woman Against a Background of Wheat
paintings.why: A woman in a straw hat stands in front of a golden field of wheat, painted with bold, swirling lines. Van Gogh painted the portrait in 1890 in Auvers-sur-Oise. The yellow and blue colors seem to vibrate. It's a happy tribute to the working people he admired.

paintings.t: Pont Boieldieu in Rouen, Rainy Weather
paintings.why: A busy city bridge crosses a river in the rain, with umbrellas, wagons and gray sky. Pissarro painted it from a hotel window in Rouen, France. The wet gray colors reflect the weather. It's a lively picture of everyday life in the rain.

A young woman tries to tie a white scarf around her sweetheart's arm to save him from danger, but he gently pulls it off to stay true to his faith. Millais painted it in 1852, based on a historical story of religious conflict in France. The emotions are visible on both faces. It was a hit with the public.

The poet Dante dreams of the death of his beloved Beatrice, who lies in a room full of flowers and angels. Rossetti painted this huge picture over several years. The colors are rich and the mood is dreamy. It's a moving image of love and loss.

A hazy blue river scene at dusk shows the Thames in London, with a barge and a dark shoreline. Whistler titled his misty twilight pictures 'Nocturnes' after music. He simplified the view to just a few soft tones. It's a masterpiece of mood and atmosphere.

A prince lies sick in bed, but a doctor discovers the cause: he's in love with his father's young wife, and his father, the king, looks on. In the story, the king gave her up for his son's sake. Ingres painted it with a lot of detail. It's a story about kindness and sacrifice.
A woman representing Truth is held up by Time, as History writes in a book. Goya painted the allegory in 1797. It means that, in time, the truth will be known. It's a hopeful idea.

A rocky mountain rises over a patchwork of fields and a viaduct, painted in blocks of blue, green and orange. Cézanne painted this mountain more than 60 times. He broke the scene into patches of color. It's one of the paintings that led to modern art.

paintings.t: The Distribution of the Eagle Standards
paintings.why: Napoleon, standing on a platform, gives his soldiers their eagle standards, with troops pledging loyalty. David painted the grand ceremony from 1804. The colors and flags are dazzling. It's a picture of power and pageantry.

In 1781, after the Battle of Yorktown, British officers lay down their arms as the American and French soldiers watch. Trumbull painted many portraits of real officers, and he worked from life. The surrender was a decisive moment in the American Revolution. It hangs in the U.S. Capitol.

A woman with a parasol and a child walk along a path in a field of red poppies, and another pair walks across the hill above. Monet painted the scene in early summer, with bright red dots of flowers. It's one of the most beloved Impressionist landscapes. It's a happy image of a sunny day.

In June 1789, members of the French National Assembly, locked out of their meeting hall, gathered in an indoor tennis court and swore to write a new constitution. David's sketch shows people with their arms raised, as curtains billow in the wind. It's a moment that started the French Revolution. It's a drawing of an idea in action.

A tall young man works at his easel, painting a still life of a bird, in a studio. Renoir painted his friend Frédéric Bazille, a fellow painter who shared his studio. It's a picture of friendship. It's a sweet look at two painters at work.

A blindfolded girl reaches out as her friends laugh and dart away, in a woodland scene. Fragonard's picture is full of the lighthearted spirit of the Rococo. The leaves and silks swirl with color. It's a delightful picture of a game.

paintings.t: Frederick the Great Playing the Flute at Sanssouci
paintings.why: King Frederick the Great plays the flute in a glittering hall lit by candles as musicians and courtiers listen. Menzel painted the king as a music-lover, which he truly was. The chandeliers and mirrors shimmer. It's a famous German painting of the 1700s.

paintings.t: Napoleon on the Battlefield of Eylau
paintings.m: Department of Paintings of the Louvre
paintings.why: Napoleon surveys the snowy field after a bloody battle in 1807, surrounded by wounded soldiers. Gros painted the horror of war along with the general's calm. It was a controversial picture that showed the cost of victory. It's a landmark of Romanticism.

The King of Spain and his queen sit with their children, in a splendid hall, in rich satins. Van Loo painted a large group portrait to display the royal family in 1743. Each member is carefully painted in elegant clothes. It's a glimpse of Spanish royalty.

paintings.t: At the Moulin Rouge, The Dance
paintings.why: Dancers kick and twirl in the Moulin Rouge nightclub while onlookers in top hats watch. Toulouse-Lautrec painted the stars of Paris nightlife, here the dancer Valentin the Boneless. He used a quick sketchy style. It's a bright picture of Parisian entertainment.

Four children in fancy clothes stand and play in a bright room: a girl does a curtsy, a boy winds up a bird organ, and a baby in a walker reaches for a cherry. Hogarth painted it for their father. A cat eyes the caged bird, and a clock has a Cupid on it. It's full of fun details.

A crowd of people in black suits and costumes, with masks and hats, are packed into a hall at the Paris Opera. Manet painted friends among the crowd. The black suits and colored costumes make a fascinating pattern. It's a picture of modern Paris at night.

A huge jagged mountain towers over a valley, as clouds swirl and a tiny house sits far below. Friedrich painted the Alps as a huge symbol of nature's power. The peaks look like they glow. It's one of his most dramatic mountain scenes.

A huge, wild crowd of masked, grinning people fills the street in a parade, with a tiny Jesus on a donkey. Ensor painted a carnival that mocked modern society. The colors are neon bright. It was shocking in 1888, and today it's regarded as a Belgian masterpiece.

A young general in a dashing uniform charges forward with a flag, determined to lead his soldiers across a bridge in Italy. Gros painted the romantic, hero's portrait of Napoleon. It was the first of many pictures that made him a legend. It's an energetic image.

A calm figure of Jesus on the cross, against a dark background, with a soft light. Goya painted it as a young man to win admission to the Academy. The body is shown in a sculptural, classical style. It's a quiet, thoughtful painting.

A young bride looks sadly away as an old official stands at her side during a wedding in a church. Pukirev's painting was a protest at forced marriages. It made a stir in Russia in 1862 and was widely discussed. It's famous as a social message in paint.

paintings.t: The Millinery Shop by Edgar Degas
paintings.why: A woman at a table in a hat shop tries a hat on a stand, with a tray of colorful hats in front. Degas shows a typical shop with unusual angles. The pale tones are soft and quiet. It's a modern view of work.

A young man leans toward a woman at a restaurant table, in the sunny garden, as a waiter looks on. Manet painted the lively scene outdoors, in bright daylight. The flirting is charming. It's a picture of Paris café life.

A woman looks out of an open window in a studio, seen from behind, toward the river and ships. Friedrich painted his wife Caroline. The picture is a metaphor for longing. It's one of the most famous images of looking out.

Farm workers pitch hay and rake in the fields under the sunny sky. Pissarro, one of the Impressionists, lived in the village of Éragny and painted its people. The colors are fresh and bright. It's a happy picture of country work.

Dante in a red robe stands on a bridge in Florence, as Beatrice walks by with her friends, not seeing him. Holiday painted a famous moment from Dante's life. It's a story of love at a distance. It's a Pre-Raphaelite-style painting.

A twisted tree branches across the canvas in a net of black lines on a gray background. Mondrian painted it in 1911 as he moved from realism toward abstraction. The branches almost become a pattern. It's a key step toward his famous grids.

A rider on a galloping horse dashes through a bright meadow, in blue cloak and dots of color. Kandinsky's painting inspired the name of the art group 'Der Blaue Reiter' (The Blue Rider). The figure is almost abstract. It's a landmark of modern art.

A sculptor and his wife stand together, with calm, long faces, in a simple background. Modigliani painted his friend Jacques Lipchitz, a sculptor, and his bride, Berthe. They paid for the portrait, and Modigliani later added more work. It's a famous double portrait.

A woman with a parasol walks along a sunny beach, as the waves and sails sparkle. Monet painted the Normandy coast with fresh and feathery strokes. The sea is a blaze of blue. It's a breezy summer day.

A mother gazes tenderly at her sleeping baby in a cradle under a gauzy, see-through veil. Berthe Morisot painted her sister Edma and her niece. Morisot was a leading Impressionist and the only woman in their first exhibition in 1874. It's one of the most beloved pictures of motherhood.

A noblewoman is dragged through the snowy streets of Moscow on a sled, her chained hand raised with two fingers in a defiant sign. Surikov painted Feodosia Morozova, who was jailed in the 1600s for her faith. The crowd reacts with sorrow, mockery and awe. It's one of the greatest Russian history paintings.

A man and woman sit in a garden at a table, near orange trees in big green tubs. Caillebotte painted the sunlit garden of his family's home. The fresh sunlight and cool shade are lovely. It's a peaceful moment.

paintings.m: Royal Academy of Fine Arts of San Fernando
paintings.why: A man in a pointed hat is being judged before a court of stern officials, in a dark, gloomy hall. Goya was critical of the Spanish Inquisition, a harsh religious court. He painted it with powerful light and dark. It's a bold statement against injustice.
l: Royal Academy of Fine Arts of San Fernando

paintings.t: The Family of the Infante Don Luis
paintings.why: A prince and his family are gathered around a card table in a candlelit room, with servants and a painter in the corner. Goya painted himself on the left, almost at the prince's feet. It's a daring and informal royal portrait. It's one of his earliest great family paintings.

A small stone house with a red roof sits at a bend in a country road in Auvers, France. The gloomy title was just a local name for the building. Cézanne painted it with thick, solid strokes. It was shown at the first Impressionist exhibition in 1874.

A woman in a red robe hugs a golden box as mist and shadowy figures rise from it. In Greek myth, Pandora opens a box and lets out all the troubles of the world, but hope remains inside. Waterhouse painted the moment just before. It's a gripping image of curiosity.

A sorceress draws a circle on the ground with a wand, while a raven and a cauldron wait nearby, on a wild, stormy moor. Waterhouse painted a witch casting a spell. The rich colors give it a magical feeling. It's a famous painting of witchcraft.

A woman in a blue-green dress stands in a rich room, mixing a potion in a pot with a black cat and a bubbling cauldron. Waterhouse painted her intent look. It's a picture of magic at work. It's among his finest.

paintings.t: Miravan Breaking Open the Tomb of his Ancestors
paintings.why: A man breaks into a tomb, with his torch, in search of treasure, but finds an inscription that warns him to leave. Wright of Derby painted dramatic lighting inside a gloomy vault. It's based on a story from a popular book. It's a haunting scene.

paintings.t: Earthstopper on the Banks of the Derwent
paintings.why: A man with a lantern and a shovel works by moonlight, blocking fox dens before a hunt. Wright painted a moonlit scene on the Derwent river in England, with a glowing moon behind the clouds. The light is magic. It's an unusual picture of rural work.

A man in prison sits with his head in his hands, in a dark cell lit by a single lamp. This is an illustration from a story by Laurence Sterne about a man who is imprisoned. Wright used the light to create a sad, quiet drama. It's a thoughtful work about freedom.

A river sparkles in the pink twilight, with a monastery and wooded banks, as the sound of bells seems to echo. Levitan painted a quiet scene on the Volga in a dreamy light. The soft sky is magical. It's one of the best-loved Russian landscapes.

A lonely, wide road stretches across a gloomy plain under a gray sky. The Vladimirka was the road along which prisoners were marched to Siberia. Levitan painted a quiet, sorrowful landscape. It's a landscape with a story of suffering.

paintings.t: Isabella and the Pot of Basil
paintings.why: A woman cradles a pot of basil, which holds a sad secret, in a rich red room. The story, from a poem by Keats, is about love and loss. Hunt painted it as a symbol of devotion. It's a famous Pre-Raphaelite painting.

A road winds through tall fields of golden rye, with towering pine trees against a bright sky. Shishkin loved the Russian countryside and painted it in great detail. The rye seems to ripple in the wind. It's a classic Russian landscape.

A young man in a suit stands with his hands in his pockets, looking down at a Paris boulevard from his balcony, seen from behind. Caillebotte painted his brother René. We can't see what he is looking at, which makes us curious. It's a famous picture of city life.

Manet sits at his easel, painting a model, while a group of his friends, including Monet and Renoir, gather to watch. Fantin-Latour painted this tribute to Manet, who was a leader of a new type of art. It's a group portrait of artists. It documents a key moment in art history.

A bright blue horse stands in a landscape of red and yellow hills, with its head bent. Franz Marc used blue to represent strength and spirit. He believed animals were closer to nature than humans. It's one of the most famous expressionist paintings.

A white monastery sits on a green hill by a river, in a golden, quiet light. Levitan loved to paint the Russian landscape with a mood of calm. It's a place that seems out of time. It's a peaceful, spiritual scene.

A woman in a green dress plays the violin, in a bright room with a window. Rossetti painted the model Alexa Wilding with a flowing golden hair, as a musician. It's a feast of color. It's a rich portrait of music and beauty.
A woman holds a fan, with a pink rose behind her ear, her dark eyes distant. Rossetti painted the portrait with deep, rich colors. The title is Italian for 'Lady Rose.' It's an elegant picture.

A young Mary sits embroidering a lily as her mother, Anne, watches in a quiet room, with a vine outside. Rossetti painted this when he was 20, one of the first Pre-Raphaelite pictures. Every object has a symbolic meaning. It's an early, important work.

A young girl in a white dress stands in a room, in front of a vase of large flowers, looking out. Olga Boznańska was a Polish painter who worked in Paris. Her soft, gray tones are very special. It's one of the best-known Polish portraits.

A woman reads in the dappled shade of a lilac tree in bloom, as the spring light falls. Monet painted it in 1872 at Argenteuil with his wife as the model. The pink blossoms and green leaves glow. It's a lovely picture of spring.

paintings.t: Symphony in White, No. 2: The Little White Girl
paintings.why: A young woman in a white dress leans at a mantelpiece, looking into a mirror, with a Japanese fan and a flower pot. Whistler painted Joanna Hiffernan, as a study in white. He named the picture like music. It's a famous work of the Aesthetic Movement.

A bride, surrounded by attendants, lifts her veil, as a young Black child offers a bouquet of flowers. Rossetti painted this scene inspired by a Bible poem. It's rich with colors and details. It's one of his finest.

paintings.m: Art Gallery of New South Wales
paintings.why: A young man wakes in a forest and sees a sleeping girl, and he is changed forever by love. Leighton painted a scene from a story by Boccaccio. The golden light and rich colors are beautiful. It's a lush picture of a magical moment.
l: Art Gallery of New South Wales

paintings.why: A calm, blue night with a glowing, shimmering sea and a few stars, and a pair of faint figures on the shore. Munch painted this in 1893, before Van Gogh's version was famous. The swirling blue sky is full of mood. It's a lesser-known night scene.

A woman in a shimmering, silky gown leans back in a chair, with a calm and slightly amused look. Sargent painted Gertrude Agnew, and the picture made him a sensation in London. The fresh and daring style was new. It's one of the most famous portraits of the 1890s.

paintings.t: Summer Evening at Skagen Beach – The Artist and his Wife
paintings.why: A couple walks along the beach at dusk, as the sea and the sky glow in tones of blue. Krøyer painted himself and his wife Marie in the soft evening light of northern Denmark. The 'blue hour' of Scandinavia is a magical time. It's a lovely, gentle scene.

Through an open window, you can see the rooftops and the harbor of Copenhagen, on a sunny day. Martinus Rørbye painted it in a clear and precise way. It's an unusual 'window picture,' which fits inside and outside in one. It's a charming early Danish painting.

The king's favorite stands in a silky gown covered in bows and flowers, in a garden room with books and a mirror. Boucher painted her as a patron of the arts, with books beside her. She was one of the most powerful women in France. It's a stylish picture.

paintings.t: Summer Evening on Skagen's Southern Beach
paintings.why: Women in white dresses walk together along the beach in the dusk, with the soft blue sea and sky. Krøyer's friends are the models. The calm, glowing colors are magical. It's a favorite Danish painting.

paintings.m: Museum of Fine Arts of Nancy
paintings.why: A young woman in a fur-trimmed coat and a hat stands in the autumn sunshine, looking at us with a calm expression. Manet painted this near the end of his life. The model was Méry Laurent, a friend. It's a delightful portrait.
l: Museum of Fine Arts of Nancy

paintings.t: Congregation Leaving the Reformed Church in Nuenen
paintings.why: Villagers in black walk out of a small church after a service, among bare trees. Van Gogh painted it in 1884–85, when his father was the pastor there. The sad dark colors reflect the winter mood. It's a painting of his early life.
A bright blue kingfisher sits on a branch beside the water, painted with strokes of color. Van Gogh loved the glowing colors of birds. It's a small, quick study. It's a charming animal portrait.

Three women in fine dresses walk down a country lane, as a cow and a girl stand by. Courbet painted his sisters as the village ladies, giving alms to a peasant girl. The picture was criticized for showing ordinary folks as large as life. It's a landmark of Realism.

paintings.t: At the French Windows. The Artist's Wife
paintings.why: A woman stands by a window, in a quiet room with a calm light, seen from behind. Ring, a Danish painter, painted his wife Sigrid. The picture feels peaceful and still. It's a famous Danish interior.

paintings.m: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design
paintings.why: A frozen fjord lies below snowy mountains, under a cold, blue-gray sky. J. C. Dahl, a Norwegian painter, painted nature with great accuracy. He was among the first to paint Norway's wild scenery. It's a famous landscape.
l: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design

paintings.why: A twilight scene of a silent fjord, with dark trees and a pale pink sky, as the night sun stays low. Slott-Møller painted the magical light of a northern summer night. The picture is hushed and dreamy. It's a favorite Danish landscape.

A woman in armor stands before the flag of a united Germany, wearing a crown, and holding a sword. Veit painted this in 1848 during a revolution when Germans hoped for a unified country. It hung in Frankfurt's parliament. It's a symbol of national hope.

George Washington looks out calmly, with a pale background left unfinished. Gilbert Stuart painted this in 1796, and it's the image of Washington on the U.S. one-dollar bill. Stuart never finished it, so he kept it and made copies. It's perhaps the most reproduced portrait in American history.

Three white children sit with a young Black boy named Bélizaire, an enslaved child who was part of their household in New Orleans. Jacques Amans painted this in 1837. Today the painting is studied for what it shows about slavery in America, because Bélizaire is one of few enslaved children painted by name. It reminds us that art can record difficult parts of history.

A woman in a light-colored dress steps out of a cheap Paris café, holding a guitar and eating cherries, with a thoughtful look. Manet saw a real street singer and asked her to pose in his studio. He treated her with the same dignity as a society lady. It's a famous picture of everyday life in Paris.

A Spanish dancer in a glittering, spangled skirt strikes a proud pose. Manet painted Lola Melea when she came to Paris with a Spanish troupe in 1862. The sparkling outfit and bold stance are eye-catching. The poet Baudelaire wrote a verse for the frame.

paintings.t: Portrait of Monsieur and Madame Auguste Manet
paintings.why: The artist's parents sit stiffly in a dark room, his father in a chair and his mother at a table with her sewing. Manet painted them early in his career, with deep care. The calm, serious faces reveal their characters. It's a quiet and moving family portrait.

paintings.m: Department of Paintings of the Louvre
paintings.why: An ancient Roman bridge with a broken arch crosses a gorge, in clean sunlight with a hill town above. Corot painted it on the spot in Italy, as a young artist. The solid shapes and gentle light are remarkable. It's one of the most admired landscape sketches of the 1800s.

A young woman in a straw hat and a blue dress sits on a rocky coast, her hands in her lap, with a soft smile. Renoir painted her at the beach in Guernsey, in a gentle, feathery style. The warm tones glow. It's one of his best portraits.

paintings.t: Nocturne: Blue and Gold – Old Battersea Bridge
paintings.why: A long wooden bridge rises as a shadowy silhouette in the dusk, with fireworks and a tiny boat below. Whistler was inspired by Japanese prints and used simple shapes and subtle tones. He painted the London night like a piece of music. It's a famous atmospheric painting.

The great German writer Goethe reclines in a traveler's cloak and a wide hat, by a ruin in the Italian countryside. Tischbein painted his friend during their trip to Italy. The pose looks like an ancient hero. It's the most famous portrait of Goethe.

A massive iceberg rises from a cold, calm sea, with a ship's broken mast lying in the foreground. Church sailed to the Arctic to sketch the real ice. When shown in New York, people paid to see this panorama. It's one of the most spectacular polar landscapes.

A British officer sits in a chair, his wife leaning on him, while their children hold a toy and look at a newspaper announcing the end of the Crimean War. Millais painted a family's joy at the end of a war. The details of uniforms and toys are lovingly done. It's a heartfelt homecoming.

paintings.t: The Return of the Dove to the Ark
paintings.why: Two of Noah's sons gently hold a dove that has returned with an olive branch, a sign that the Flood is ending. Millais used a vivid red and green. The picture is bright with hope. It's a famous Pre-Raphaelite painting of a Bible story.

A beautiful woman in a black dress points to her ring, which bears Goya's name, as a wry reminder of the artist's skill. The Duchess of Alba was one of Spain's grandest ladies. Goya's portrait of her is powerful and playful. It's a famous mystery of art history.

Manet stands with his palette and brushes in a pale suit and a hat, looking out calmly. This is his only full-length self-portrait, and the style is elegant and cool. He painted it near the end of his life. It's a very stylish portrait.

A procession of women in colorful robes, with flowers, move along a marble street in an ancient festival, with the blue sea in the distance. Alma-Tadema loved to paint the warm Mediterranean world. The scene is rich in details. It's a bright vision of spring in the ancient world.
A Polish nobleman rides a rearing white horse in a fine uniform, in a heroic pose. David painted the portrait in Rome. The dramatic composition shows his skill. It's a spirited portrait.

A surgeon performs an operation in a medical amphitheater, as students lean in to watch. Eakins painted Dr. Hayes Agnew, who has just finished teaching his last class. The picture is clean and well-lit, in contrast with his earlier, darker Gross Clinic. It shows how medicine had changed.

paintings.m: Académie royale de peinture et de sculpture
paintings.why: A skate fish hangs open on a hook, a cat arches its back at the sight, and oysters lie on a kitchen table. Chardin painted this at 28, and it won him membership in the French Academy. The colors, textures and shapes are magical. It's one of the greatest still lifes ever painted.

White huts glow in the moonlight by a stream, in a deep blue night under a starry sky. Kuindzhi painted the glowing moon so brightly that people thought there was a lamp behind it. The silvery light is magical. It's a favorite Ukrainian landscape.

A couple sits at the edge of a river in the sun, with sailboats and the town of Argenteuil in the background, in bright blue. Manet painted it outdoors in 1874, following the Impressionists. The colors are fresh and the mood is cheerful. It's one of his boldest paintings.

paintings.m: Herbert F. Johnson Museum of Art
paintings.why: A young country girl with a stick stands barefoot with a flock of geese in a field. Bouguereau painted peasant girls in soft light. The smooth skin and bright colors are typical of his charm. It's a delightful and sweet picture.
l: Herbert F. Johnson Museum of Art

paintings.why: Two old men in a dark room, one gaunt and one hunched over a bowl, with strange, shadowy faces. Goya painted this on a wall in his house. It is one of the 'Black Paintings' that he made for himself. It's a strange and powerful image.

A woman in a dark red velvet dress with a gold shawl sits in an elegant pose, her cheeks flushed, in front of a mirror. Ingres painted the fine details of fabrics, hair and jewelry. The critics found the picture odd at the time, but it's now admired. It's one of his greatest portraits.

A boy leans on a table, watching a bubble he's made, with a skull nearby that reminds us that life is short. Manet painted it as a 'vanitas,' a type of picture about how things are fragile. The boy is Léon Leenhoff, his stepson. It's a thoughtful picture about time.

paintings.t: Claude Monet painting in his studio boat
paintings.why: Monet sits on his floating studio, painting while his wife Camille sits in the cabin. Manet painted his friend at work on the river Seine at Argenteuil. They painted together in the open air. It's a picture of one great painter looking at another.

Near the end of the American Civil War, President Lincoln and three leaders meet on a steamship to discuss peace. Healy painted the scene a few years after, in a quiet cabin with a view of the sea. The painting honors the hope for peace. It hangs in the White House.

paintings.t: The Fight Between Mars and Minerva
paintings.m: Académie royale de peinture et de sculpture
paintings.why: The god of war, Mars, battles the goddess of wisdom, Minerva, as Venus tries to help. David painted this as a student and won a prize in Paris. It's a lesson that wisdom defeats brute force. It's an early peek at his talent.

paintings.t: A View through Three of the North-Western Arches of the Third Storey of the Coliseum
paintings.why: The huge stone arches of the Colosseum in Rome frame a sunlit view of the city. Eckersberg, a Danish painter, painted it on a visit to Italy. The light and the shadow on the stone are exact. It's a classic Danish painting.

A pair of worn leather boots with muddy laces sits on the floor. Van Gogh painted several pictures of old boots, finding beauty in them. The philosopher Heidegger wrote about them. It's an ordinary thing that tells a story about a hard-working life.

A man in a hat strolls through Paris with two little girls and a dog, in a quick, candid scene. Degas painted Viscount Lepic, who was a friend and a fellow artist. It looks like a snapshot. It's a lively view of the city.

paintings.m: Department of Paintings of the Louvre
paintings.why: The pope sits wearing a red cape, looking weary, and he rests his hands on a chair. David painted it in Paris before Napoleon's coronation. The face is full of character. It's among the best portraits of its day.

A fireman carries three small children out of a burning house, as the mother kneels in thankfulness. Millais painted the glowing flames. The painting was a favorite for its drama. It's a thrilling image of bravery.
A bullfighter lies in the sand, in a black suit, shot in the ring. Manet cut a figure from a larger picture. The soft grays and blacks are painted with great skill. It's a quiet and striking picture.

paintings.m: KODE Art museums and composer homes
paintings.why: A crowd of people in dark clothes, with pale, mask-like faces, walks toward us along a main street in Oslo, with a single man going the other way. Munch painted the feeling of being alone in a crowd. The strange lights make it eerie. It's an early step toward his famous anxiety paintings.

Ships rest at the harbor of Friedrich's hometown, with the town's church spires against a glowing sky. He painted his birthplace from memory. The sky is a soft, golden blue. It's a calm and lovely harbor view.

A group of artists and writers, including Manet and Whistler, gather around a portrait of the painter Delacroix. Fantin-Latour painted it to honor Delacroix, who had recently died. It's like a family photo. It shows who the leading artists of the day were.

Priestesses and visitors gather around a bronze bowl to hear a prophecy in an ancient Greek temple. Waterhouse studied ancient art to get the details right. The women lean in with awe. It's an atmospheric picture of ancient belief.

paintings.t: Max Schmitt in a Single Scull
paintings.why: A rower glides across the Schuylkill River in Philadelphia in the early morning, as a tiny figure of the artist rows in the distance. Eakins painted his friend, who was a champion. The sunlight on the water is gorgeous. It's among the first great American sports paintings.

The queen of France holds a rose in her hand in a simple dress and a straw hat, in a garden. Vigée Le Brun painted her as a lovely woman instead of a queen. The first version was shocking because it was so informal. It's a very charming portrait.

paintings.t: A Cotton Office in New Orleans
paintings.why: Men in a busy office examine samples of cotton, read newspapers and talk business. Degas painted the office of his uncle during a trip to New Orleans. It's an unusual picture of work. It's also a reminder that cotton was a huge industry that depended on enslaved labor before the Civil War.

paintings.t: Maison devant la Sainte-Victoire près de Gardanne (House in Provence)
paintings.why: A group of orange-roofed houses sits in front of the mountain in the south of France, in blocks of color. Cézanne painted the village of Gardanne, simplifying the buildings into cubes. Some people say this led to Cubism. It's a pioneering piece.
